item.title: 空气污染是痴呆症的一个诱因
item.description: 根据发表在《Journal of Neuroinflammation》期刊上的一项研究，微小的空气污染颗粒可能会通过改变大脑免疫细胞的行为对大脑造成损害。研究结果表明空气污染是痴呆症的一个诱因。研究人员分析了英国生物样本库（UK Biobank）约 50 万名成年人的数据；该研究数据集对参与者的健康状况进行了长达 14 年的追踪。结果发现，相比生活在污染程度最低的三分之一地区的人群，居住在污染程度最高的三分之一地区的人群，患阿尔茨海默病或相关痴呆症的风险高 25%。在排除了年龄、吸烟、糖尿病等因素的影响后，这一结论依然成立。无论个人患阿尔茨海默病的遗传风险高低，空气污染都会增加其患病风险。研究团队对小鼠展开了进一步实验，让小鼠暴露在污染空气中五个月。结果发现健康的小鼠出现了记忆障碍、血脑屏障受损以及大脑炎症。研究还发现，空气污染改变了小胶质细胞基因的激活状态，干扰了大脑免疫细胞的正常功能。

item.title: 英伟达CEO黄仁勋“凤还巢”台股创单日最大涨幅 台湾民众支持查间谍疑云
item.description: 美国芯片巨头英伟达(NVIDIA，台湾称辉达)执行长黄仁勋的复职在他的出生地台湾掀起一片欢呼。台北股市星期二(11月24日)开出庆祝行情，一举突破4万点创下单日最大涨幅。黄仁勋的回归甚至还牵动了这个周末即将举行的台湾地方选举的选情。

item.title: 基因工程烟草能用于高效合成抗癌药
item.description: 紫杉醇（paclitaxel）是临床上应用最广泛的化疗药物之一，被大量用于治疗乳腺癌、卵巢癌和肺癌等多种恶性肿瘤。然而这种救命药最初提取自太平洋红豆杉的树皮，天然含量极低。科学家正在尝试把红豆杉合成紫杉醇的基因全部搬到生长迅速的其他植物或微生物中，像酿酒或种庄稼一样，低成本、可持续地批量生产紫杉醇。一项研究在本氏烟草（Nicotiana benthamiana）中首次完整重构并验证了紫杉醇的从头生物合成途径，使工程烟草中的紫杉醇产量飙升 500 倍以上，达到与天然红豆杉树皮相当的水平。本氏烟草是普通烟草的近亲，但它通常不被用来制作香烟，而因为生长周期短、容易进行基因工程而成为生物科学研究中的重要植物。

item.title: 黄仁勋重返英伟达，为什么反转来得这么快？
item.description:
2026-11-24 22:13:33

2025年7月23日，美国华盛顿特区，黄仁勋出席“赢得AI竞赛”活动（图：视觉中国）

没有人能想象一位手握全球AI命脉、坐在权力王座的CEO，会如此戏剧性地突然离场。更无法想象，他会在短短11天后重新回到王座。

当地时间11月23日，英伟达发布公告：董事会一致投票通过，恢复黄仁勋总裁、首席执行官及董事职务。黄仁勋就复职发表声明说：“我很荣幸回到英伟达，在新的工业革命开始时领导世界上最具影响力的科技公司之一。我迫不及待地想回去工作。”

消息一出，美股市场和AI行业立刻沸腾，英伟达股价一度暴涨超30%。当天，黄仁勋重新回到位于美国加州圣克拉拉的公司总部，员工聚集在总部大厅的楼梯和走廊旁鼓掌欢呼，他为自己犯下的严重错误给员工带来的动荡表示歉意。“感谢大家给我第二次机会。我会成为一个更好的CEO。”

英伟达董事会主席琼斯在当天的声明中表示：“董事会认为，黄仁勋是领导英伟达的合适人选，恢复他的职务符合股东、员工、合作伙伴以及客户的最大利益。”

声明称，董事会在决策过程中听取了美国政府高层的意见，并认为黄仁勋复职不存在国家安全风险。

短时间内剧情反转的背后，究竟是怎样复杂的政治博弈？重掌英伟达的黄仁勋，将面临哪些前所未有的复杂命题？《南方人物周刊》采访了中国社会科学院美国研究所研究员、美国政治研究室主任刘卫东和复旦大学中国研究院特任副研究员刘典，听他们解析黄仁勋闪电离职和复职背后的原因。

2026年9月29日，美国华盛顿特区，美国总统特朗普（前排右）在白宫东厅与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋（前排左）及科技行业高管会面，讨论人工智能相关议题（图：视觉中国）

政治斗争的“棋子”？

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋短短11天后就回归英伟达，这些天里究竟出现了什么新变量？

刘典：这11天实际上是一次对黄仁勋不可替代性的压力测试。11月17日，英伟达董事长还明确表示不会重新任命黄仁勋；11月23日，董事会却一致同意其复职。其间有三个变量发生变化：

一是员工、投资者和产业伙伴的支持逐渐形成公开压力，马斯克等科技界人士也加入声援；

二是资本市场重新评估创始人离任的成本，复职消息公布后英伟达股价单日上涨约31.5%，市值增加约9500亿美元，虽然不能把全部涨幅归因于个人，但足以说明市场对领导层不确定性非常敏感；

三是美国政府高层直接介入，董事会公告明确将政府意见作为判断复职安全风险的依据。

值得注意的是，英伟达11月17日公布的季度营收达到1160亿美元，说明公司并没有因为黄仁勋离任而立即丧失经营能力。真正难以替代的是他对未来的组织能力：协调供应链、客户、技术路线与资本投入。董事会最终面对的不是一家经营失灵的企业，而是一家经营强劲、却难以迅速复制创始人战略协调能力的企业。

南方人物周刊：博弈一般是一个长期的过程，为什么解职与复职在时间上只有短短11天？

刘卫东：归根结底是股市崩盘了，影响太大。从稳定国内市场、稳定民心的角度来说，大家都喊着黄仁勋必须回来。他带来的问题远远少于他能提供的帮助。

黄仁勋离任的主要原因是不正当关系，对国家安全的可能伤害并未确认。在美国政坛上，如果一个企业家如此不可或缺，失去他，一个至关重要的核心产业都可能停滞。那在这样的背景下，他犯的个人错误已经不算什么事了。

英伟达高层，以及以商务部长为代表的力量，本来是反对（他复职）的，但在全社会的压力之下——英伟达员工的压力、其他科技右翼领袖人物的压力、特朗普政府的压力，尤其是经济和股市方面的压力传导过来以后，他们就没有办法拒绝了。

南方人物周刊：有观点认为黄仁勋是政治斗争的棋子？

刘卫东：我觉得不能这么明确地下这个判断。背后的斗争，首先是《纽约时报》这类以自由派为主的媒体先挖出了黄仁勋的所谓劣迹，随后社会舆论把压力压到他身上。

他一开始并不想辞职，但舆论越来越大，他不得不辞职。所以首先是社会舆论倒逼英伟达高层向黄仁勋施压，因为黄仁勋跟（现任）美国政府绑定得很深，开始主要是社会力量在对政府施压，民主党是随后才介入的。

刘典：我不认为可以把黄仁勋简单理解为政治斗争的棋子。他既受到政治约束，也是能够影响产业议程的企业家。

英伟达已经从一家芯片公司成长为美国人工智能基础设施的重要组织者，其经营稳定性牵动云计算企业、数据中心建设、资本市场和半导体供应链。特朗普公开推动其复职，体现了产业竞争力、市场稳定与安全监管之间的政策权衡，但不能据此认定所有调查或争议都是政治操弄。

南方人物周刊：特朗普为什么要力保黄仁勋？

刘卫东：黄仁勋是特朗普的私人好友，他认为芯片是大国竞争的核心产业，而黄仁勋无人可替代。从私人和党派角度，黄仁勋对特朗普都有很大的正面价值，可以说是一个“工具”或者“助手”。所以，特朗普会千方百计保护黄仁勋。

特朗普的立场并非一以贯之，他中间犹豫过、摇摆过，只不过保护黄仁勋的想法最终战胜了让他下台的想法，权衡各种机会、挫折和收益之后，（特朗普）坚定地站在了黄仁勋这一边。

2026年11月23日，美国纽约证券交易所，一块屏幕上播放着英伟达公司恢复黄仁勋首席执行官职务的消息（图：视觉中国）

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋复职，还有哪些考量？

刘典：从商业角度来看，黄仁勋的价值在于协调全球产业链，而不只是管理公司内部。他能够把台积电等上游制造伙伴、云服务商、模型开发者和资本市场的预期连接起来。

在AI资本开支巨大、投资回报受到审视的阶段，这种协调能力尤其稀缺。复职可以降低短期战略的不确定性，却不会自动解决资金循环、投资回报和出口合规的问题。英伟达董事会仍然推进独立调查，也说明经营需要与责任认定并未合并为一个问题。

南方人物周刊：民主党会就此罢休吗？接下来会采取哪些措施？

刘卫东：民主党肯定不会善罢甘休。现在已经开始了，他们指责特朗普政府和英伟达高层说变就变、没有任何原则，在没搞清楚黄仁勋事件是否危害美国国家安全的前提下就要求他复职。

可以想象，下一届国会就职以后一定会拿此事进行大范围调查，希望找到特朗普政府利用不合法、不合规手段向英伟达施压、帮助黄仁勋复职的证据。

南方人物周刊：民主党争夺的是AI发展方向和监管政策的主导权吗？

刘卫东：民主党更看重监管，特朗普政府更看重发展。所以，民主党不是要争夺主导权，而是要加强监管。

民主党今后的针对目标很可能不仅是黄仁勋，而是整个AI发展思路，他们与特朗普政府目前放任自流的想法是截然对立的。下一届国会就职后，人工智能治理一定会成为民主党重点关注的领域。

他们本身也需要发展人工智能、需要跟他国竞争，但民主党历来关注垄断问题，国家安全本来是共和党更关注的。现在共和党掌控白宫，民主党也开始关注国家安全，目的其实是为给对手找麻烦。

今后一段时间，白宫与国会之间、民主党控制的地方州与联邦之间，在AI监管问题上都会进行更多斗争。

英伟达的权力重构与算力博弈

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋没有超级投票权，仅持股3.58%，董事会6票就可以把他投出局？

刘典：这里必须区分股权控制、法定经营权限和事实上的战略影响力。黄仁勋没有超级投票权，不能凭约3.6%的股份单方面决定董事会构成或任免结果；但具体需要多少票，应根据章程、出席人数及适用程序判断，不能简单认定固定6票即可将其赶出公司。此次官方口径也是辞职获董事会接受，而非已经证实的强制罢免。

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋在制度上没有实际控制权，先被公司制度赶走、又被程序请回，董事会的信誉会大打折扣吗？这暴露了公司治理的哪些问题？

刘典：真正暴露的是一种治理悖论：董事会具有更换CEO的制度权力，却未必具备承受更换CEO的后果及此后的组织能力。

先明确拒绝复职，数日后又一致同意其复职，必然使市场追问决策依据为何变化、政府意见发挥了什么作用、独立调查与经营判断如何隔离。如果董事会能够充分说明新证据和决策程序，调整决定本身未必是治理失败；但如果重大决策高度依赖外部压力，又缺乏充分解释，就会损害治理的可预期性。

英伟达需要建设的不是一个更难被罢免的CEO，而是一套既能约束创始人、又能在其缺席时持续运行的治理体系。

2026年10月21日，德国柏林，黄仁勋在英伟达GTC大会上展示Spectrum-X 以太网（图：NVIDIA）

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋回归，会不会像OpenAI首席执行官山姆·奥特曼闪电回归一样，重组董事会和核心管理层？

刘典：两次事件的共同点，是正式治理权与创始人的实际组织影响力发生碰撞，员工、资本与产业伙伴的态度改变了治理决策的外部条件。但OpenAI在2023年经历的是非营利治理结构与商业化组织之间的冲突，英伟达则是成熟的上市公司，其董事会还受到证券监管、受托责任和出口合规等约束，不能直接套用OpenAI模式。

目前更值得观察的不是董事会是否全面换血，而是权力是否重新分配。11月23日的公告明确，哈维·琼斯继续担任董事长，克雷斯继续担任CFO，新设国家安全与出口管制委员会，并启动首席合规官招聘，后者向董事会的提名与公司治理委员会报告。

这些安排表明，黄仁勋恢复经营领导权的同时，独立监督机制正在强化。未来即使出现个别董事或高管调整，也应区分正常组织优化与创始人重新集中权力。目前尚无充分证据认定黄仁勋将全面改组董事会。

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋复职后还将面临哪些与从前不同的复杂问题？

刘卫东：首先是在英伟达内部建立安全评估体系，什么样的芯片能卖给什么样的人，这必须要做，原则上要进一步限制。第二是技术限制：如何保证某些芯片出口第三国后，不会被转卖给美国的竞争对手。技术上，各界包括特朗普政府都会对英伟达提出要求。

个人层面，黄仁勋会面临民主党的一些挑战和调查要求：他跟特朗普究竟是什么关系，有没有可能为满足特朗普需求而抛弃美国国家利益。外部会面临很多问题。特朗普也要求他正式道歉后再回归CEO的位置。他需要对今后的个人行为约束作出表态，需要家庭出来支持他、表示理解和宽容。

刘典：黄仁勋回归后的最大变化，是英伟达的商业决策可能面临更强的国家安全审查与合规约束。过去公司主要在技术迭代、客户需求、供应链保障之间寻找平衡，未来还要更系统地处理出口许可、第三国数据中心、最终用户核查以及跨境服务的合规风险。与此同时，相关调查、证券诉讼与AI基础设施投资回报问题并未因复职而消失。公司需要在市场扩张与风险控制之间建立更加明确的制度边界。

南方人物周刊：黄仁勋回归后，中美算力博弈会发生哪些变化？

刘典：中美算力博弈正在从芯片所有权竞争延伸到算力使用权、软件生态与智能生产成本竞争。

黄仁勋过去支持保持一定的对华商业联系，但其回归不意味着美国出口管制必然放松。中国更应关注规则变化带来的长期不确定性，加快国产算力与开放模型、推理框架、行业应用的协同适配。未来衡量竞争力不能只看单卡的峰值性能，还应看同等任务质量下的单位词元成本、系统稳定性和迁移成本。

真正的战略主动权，不是等待英伟达内部出现变化，而是建立能够持续、经济地生产智能服务的自主产业生态。

item.title: 今天，国际航天合作掀开全新一页
item.description:
过去很多年，由美俄等国牵头建造和运营的国际空间站是太空中唯一的“人类实验室”，全球南方国家几乎没有机会摸到它的门槛。中国过去也长期被美国“沃尔夫条款”排除在外，当年没有拿到国际空间站“入场券”的中国，靠自力更生开出了自己的“太空班车”，也为其他国家留出了“座位”


北京时间11月25日上午，神舟二十四号载人飞船将在酒泉卫星发射中心发射。备受国际舆论关注的，是本次飞行乘组中出现了第一个“非中国面孔”。来自巴基斯坦的航天员穆罕默德·齐尚·阿里将与中国航天员一道到访“天宫”，完成中国载人航天工程史上首次中外航天员联合飞行，他还将承担中巴合作空间科学实验任务。巴媒纷纷以“历史性飞行”“2.5亿巴基斯坦人的希望”等为标题进行报道，中国网友也以“星河共逢八方客，天宫遥聚四海宾”表示欢迎。一条由中国携手全球南方国家共同开辟的合作航道，正在浩瀚太空徐徐铺展。


7个月前，阿里走进中国航天员中心。用他自己的话说，他带来了2.5亿巴基斯坦人的期望。众所周知，载人航天对工业基础、科研实力与资金投入的要求极高，绝大多数全球南方国家难以独自跨越。尽管1967年生效的《外空条约》早已明确，外空探测及使用“应造福于各国人民”，不论他们的经济或科学发展程度如何，“不得有任何歧视”。但在过去很多年，由美俄等国牵头建造和运营的国际空间站是太空中唯一的“人类实验室”，全球南方国家几乎没有机会摸到它的门槛。


“巴铁”第一个进入“天宫”，是两国36年航天合作水到渠成的结果。早在1990年，巴基斯坦首颗科学实验卫星Badr-1搭乘中国火箭升空，此后双方合作逐步延伸至通信、遥感、卫星导航等领域；2024年，巴基斯坦立方星随嫦娥六号奔月，实现该国首次月球探测；如今巴基斯坦即将圆载人航天之梦，其月球车项目也已入选嫦娥八号国际合作清单。中巴航天合作的步步深入，是全球南方合作向科技前沿拓展的生动注脚——全球南方国家要改善民生、推进工业化，同样也有攀登科技高峰的权利与梦想。


回望中国载人航天的发展之路，这份开放姿态更显珍贵。中国曾因外部政治因素无法参加国际空间站建设，美国出台的“沃尔夫条款”，更明确把中国排除在合作对象之外。但正因为自己淋过雨，所以更想为别人撑把伞。早在“天宫”建成前，中国便“不附加条件地”向世界发出合作邀约，与联合国外层空间事务办公室共同遴选出首批国际科研项目，涉及17个国家的23家科研机构。此次阿里也是作为载荷专家承担实打实的科研任务。当年没有拿到国际空间站“入场券”的中国，靠自力更生开出了自己的“太空班车”，也为其他国家留出了“座位”。


对于“天宫”来说，这也是一个新的开始，更多国家特别是全球南方国家可以携手搭建“朋友圈”。除了载人航天，中国已将嫦娥六号采集的人类首批月背月壤样品正式赠送联合国，北斗卫星导航系统为140余个国家和地区“指南”，中国—巴西地球资源卫星守护着亚马孙热带雨林，中国还与50多个国家和国际组织签署超200份航天合作协议……上个世纪强权太空争霸的旧格局已经翻篇，国际航天合作掀开历史性的崭新一页。


如今外空已成为人类经济社会发展的新疆域，外空开发利用与规则制定，直接关乎各国长远利益。10月23日，中方发布《关于加强外空治理的中国立场》，明确提出维护各国公平进入外空、不受歧视地探索和利用外空的权利，提升发展中国家代表性和发言权。倘若广大全球南方国家长期缺席外空探索，未来外空资源分配、产业规则制定的话语权，岂不是又要被少数国家牢牢攥在手里？人类向外空拓展生存发展空间，不该把地球上的南北鸿沟复制到外空，更不能让这片新疆域沦为少数国家独享红利的“自留地”。


“欲穷千里目，更上一层楼。”这是阿里在中国训练期间格外喜爱的一句古诗。过去，人们习惯于用航天器飞得多远、航天员在轨驻留多久来衡量航天事业的进步。或许还可以加上一个尺度，那就是人类已经走过的这段太空征途，有多少国家能够参与、有多少人的梦想能够在其中实现。太空不是少数国家的专属竞技场，每个怀揣梦想的国家，都有权利追逐自己的星辰大海。



本文系环球时报社评

item.title: 德克萨斯州民主党选举获胜，华人社区希望废除限制购房租房的法律
item.description:
德克萨斯州民主党在11月中期选举中赢得州长、州检察长和联邦参议员等关键职位。三名当选者此前都曾反对SB17，反对该法的华人组织因此希望新政府推动废除，或至少修改对移民影响最大的条款。 SB17以国家安全为由，限制与中国、俄罗斯、伊朗和朝鲜有关的个人及实体在德州购买房地产和签订一年及以上租约。支持者认为这有助于防范外国势力取得土地，反对者则批评法律措辞模糊，使部分中国留学生、工作签证持有人难以判断自己能否租房或购房。 律师指出，长期租赁限制可能影响中国企业租用办公场所，进而妨碍新设美国办事处满足L-1签证申请要求。相关法律挑战案件目前正在联邦地区法院等待审前程序。 华人社区还担心，法律会削弱德州对国际人才和企业的吸引力。围绕SB17的持续动员则促使更多华人参与选举和公共事务。

来源

item.title: 金融时报：日本首相高市早苗在世界外交舞台上孤立无援
item.description:
一名驻东京的外交官说：“我认为，不能责怪其他国家没有站出来支持日本。” 这名外交官表示：“真正重要的是，习近平成功地让日本在亚太峰会上显得不那么重要，并且让高市早苗被排除在主要领导人的行列之外。日本可能不得不逐渐习惯这样的处境。” 早稻田大学的中林美惠子认为，高市早苗自身的外交表现同样存在问题。她既没有充分开展外交活动，也未能展现出团结中等强国、建立国家联盟的能力。 中林美惠子说：“她本来可以在APEC会议期间与更多国家领导人会面，但她没有充分利用这些机会。她应该抓住每一个会晤机会，却没有这样做。” 她表示：“结果就是，没有人知道她的外交目标究竟是什么。她很擅长面对日本国内的受众，但她没有让其他国家了解日本究竟在奉行什么样的战略。” 分析人士认为，这次APEC会议几乎没有带来任何令人乐观的迹象，无法让人相信中日两国很快就能解决分歧。

来源

item.title: 人工智能相关岗位将继续增加，成为2027年美国招聘市场的重要趋势
item.description:
ZipRecruiter对数百名招聘经理的调查显示，67%的美国企业计划在2027年增加招聘人数，高于2026年的63%。30%的企业认为人工智能将推动招聘增加，较上一年的19%上升。 人工智能相关人才的需求正从科技行业扩展至整个经济领域。调查显示，企业更愿意为掌握人工智能技能的人才支付更高薪酬，但只有21%的企业预计人工智能会导致明年岗位减少。 专业和商业服务行业在2026年前十个月增加了23.2万个就业岗位，扭转了2024年和2025年的下降趋势。ZipRecruiter经济学家妮可·巴肖认为，2027年的招聘环境可能是过去几年来最好的，但年轻人求职仍可能困难，劳动者也不应期待明显加薪。 巴肖还表示，如果出现合适机会，多达四分之一的劳动者希望换工作；招聘市场一旦重新活跃，长期受压抑的跳槽需求可能推高主动离职人数。

来源

item.title: 东北积雪天数预计将会显著减少
item.description: 根据两项研究，未来东北地积雪覆盖天数将普遍减少。与 2001 年—2020 年相比，到本世纪末，中等排放情景下区域平均积雪覆盖天数预计减少约 64 天，低排放和高排放情景下分别减少约 42天 和 85 天。高排放情景下，年积雪覆盖不足 50 天的区域占比预计由 19% 增至 99%，表明大范围地区可能向短暂、间歇性积雪状态转变。研究进一步指出，未来雪季缩短具有明显的季节非对称性。雪季前期积雪变化主要与降雪条件相关，而冬末至春季积雪持续性对升温更为敏感，其损失成为较强增暖情景下雪季缩短的突出特征。

item.title: 马来西亚总理：中国非常理性；与中国打交道比与美国更容易
item.description:
据《南华早报》11月24日报道，马来西亚总理安瓦尔在接受该报专访时表示，由于马来西亚与中国存在长期的文化和地区联系，与北京打交道总体上比与华盛顿打交道更容易。此外，中国更愿意花时间倾听、理解马来西亚的关切。他表示，马来西亚政府不会在中国与美国间选边站队。


在采访中，安瓦尔表示，中国也从未要求马来西亚在中美之间“选边站”，也从未阻碍马来西亚与美国达成任何技术合作安排。“与中国保持良好关系，并不妨碍我们继续与美国交往。中国似乎也理解这一点。”


安瓦尔也谈及中马两国在南海问题上的对话。他评价中国“非常理性”，只要双方尊重彼此在一些核心敏感问题上的立场，相关对话就会继续进行。他表示，每个国家都有不愿作出妥协的“红线”，双方不触碰这些问题，并在其他问题上灵活处理。

item.title: 黄仁勋复职，美媒最新爆料
item.description:
当地时间11月23日，英伟达董事会宣布，恢复黄仁勋的总裁、首席执行官和董事职务。据多家美国媒体报道，美国总统特朗普亲自操盘推动了这一人事变动，而在这个过程中，副总统万斯发挥了关键的沟通斡旋作用。


《纽约时报》称，上周晚些时候，特朗普已经决定尽一切可能帮助黄仁勋复职。周末，特朗普又要求副总统万斯与黄仁勋沟通，并与英伟达董事会合作解决这一问题。此后，万斯在周末与黄仁勋进行了私下交谈，并帮助英伟达董事会获得了他们需要的关键保证，即特朗普政府并不认为黄仁勋构成国家安全风险。周日晚间，英伟达董事会通知特朗普政府，公司将在周一早晨股市开盘前对外宣布黄仁勋复职的消息。


“在指示万斯与黄仁勋及其同事接触时，特朗普实际上是在求助于自己政府内部与硅谷关系最密切的官员之一。”报道称，万斯与黄仁勋的一些重要支持者和仰慕者关系密切，例如投资人戴维·萨克斯，萨克斯目前担任美国总统科学技术顾问委员会联合主席，此前还曾担任特朗普在人工智能和加密货币事务方面的重要顾问。


美联社同样援引一名知情人士的话称，万斯在上周末加大了介入的力度，他代表特朗普向英伟达董事会传达了希望让黄仁勋恢复职务的立场。该人士称，白宫方面认为，万斯在进入政界前曾在硅谷工作过，也有足够的影响力，可以作为特使帮助英伟达董事会成员打消重新聘用黄仁勋的顾虑。另据韩国媒体《先驱经济》报道，万斯的一位重要政治提携者是亿万富翁投资人、PayPal和Palantir联合创始人彼得·蒂尔。万斯曾利用自己的人脉关系，为美国的政治保守派引入了大量科技行业资金。


黄仁勋复职消息公布后，万斯在社交平台X上发布了一段视频片段，截取自特朗普接受CNBC采访的内容。特朗普在其中肯定了万斯的作用，并表示自己曾与很多人讨论黄仁勋回归一事，其中包括“优秀的副总统万斯”。


“在共和党中期选举失利的第二天，万斯曾公开将共和党的败选归咎于对伊朗的战争，此举激怒了特朗普。”《先驱经济》评论称，“万斯此次在黄仁勋复职事件中发挥作用，或许为自己赢得了特朗普的一些好感。”

item.title: “终于有人说说干发帽了”上热搜，网友：原来如此！
item.description:
近日，话题“终于有人说说干发帽了”，引发大量网友讨论。



评论区中，不少网友吐槽：干发帽包久了，头发出油、闷头皮，甚至加重脱发……



还有博主测试发现，干发帽包头超过5分钟，掉发量可飙升至洗头前的3倍。这是危言耸听还是确有其事？


据扬子晚报报道，南京江北医院皮肤科副主任医师孔玉龙表示，单次或偶尔用干发帽包裹头发，不可能出现如此大量的脱发，即使是因为闷热或者细菌感染、真菌感染，也不会出现突然性的掉发。“真正需要警惕的，是长期、经常性的不良习惯，头皮被反复刺激，就会导致毛囊损伤，出现伴随脂溢性脱发的情况，这是一个缓慢积累的过程。”



干发帽本身有吸水作用，能把头发表面的水分吸走。但对于发根部位的水分，干发帽不太能吸收干净。这时如果包裹的时间太久，接近头皮的位置处在长时间的闷热潮湿环境下，会带来滋生细菌或真菌的风险。


孔玉龙说，“真菌比如马拉色菌，细菌的话就是痤疮丙酸杆菌等，都可能大量繁殖，进而引发头皮瘙痒、头屑增多、脂溢性皮炎等问题。”



浙江省中山医院中医内科副主任叶璐则表示，从中医角度看，“头为诸阳之会”，洗头后腠理开张，湿发久闷会使湿邪留滞头部、困阻阳气，进而牵连全身，更多表现为晨起头重、脖子发僵、脑袋不清爽，有的人还会诱发或加重偏头痛。


宁波市第二医院脱发门诊副主任医师刘丽琴称，使用干发帽最好不要超过5分钟，更不要戴着干发帽过夜。


她提醒，洗头后，用吸水性强、柔软的毛巾或干发帽包裹住头发轻轻按压，带走大部分水分即可，不要用力揉搓。


同时，吹头发时，注意吹风机温度不要太高，最好用低温模式。



刘丽琴建议，睡前尽量不洗头发，因为潮湿的头皮环境容易导致马拉色菌繁殖，容易头皮痒，是掉发的元凶之一。


明天起，洗头请调整一下！

记得提醒关心的人！

item.title: 英伟达股价大幅反弹，特朗普发声
item.description:
英伟达创始人黄仁勋重返公司管理层，不仅带动英伟达股价大幅反弹，也让一众科技富豪身价随之水涨船高。


据美国《福布斯》杂志网站报道，英伟达董事会11月23日一致投票同意，即日起恢复黄仁勋担任公司总裁、首席执行官（CEO）及董事会成员。而在11天前，英伟达宣布黄仁勋辞职，引发市场对公司管理层稳定性的担忧，美股人工智能板块也因此承压。


消息公布后，市场情绪迅速反转。据美国消费者新闻与商业频道（CNBC）报道，纳斯达克指数涨幅约6.51%，标准普尔500指数涨幅约4.73%。英伟达股价当天上涨39.52美元，涨幅约31.5%，单日市值暴增近万亿美元，创下美股单家公司单日市值增量纪录。


《福布斯》收盘估算数据显示，截至美股23日收盘，黄仁勋持有英伟达约3.5%股份，个人净资产单日增加339亿美元，达到约1440亿美元，在全球富豪排名回升至第13位。


埃隆·马斯克（左）与黄仁勋（资料图） 图源：外媒


实时富豪榜显示，特斯拉和太空探索技术公司（SpaceX）CEO埃隆·马斯克净资产单日增加约596亿美元；戴尔科技创始人迈克尔·戴尔增加约175亿美元；甲骨文联合创始人拉里·埃里森增加约137亿美元。谷歌联合创始人拉里·佩奇和谢尔盖·布林的净资产分别增加126亿和116亿美元。


英伟达内部的持股高管和董事会成员同样受益。公司首席财务官、短暂担任临时CEO的科莱特·克雷斯持有超过400万股英伟达股票，为高管中持股量第二位。长期董事、早期投资者马克·史蒂文斯和滕奇·考克斯也持有大量股份，几天前因股价下跌净资产各缩水约20亿美元，此次预计有所回升。


美国总统特朗普23日在接受CNBC采访时，也对英伟达股价表现发出赞叹。他说：“天哪，那东西就像一艘火箭，曾朝着错误的方向飞。现在它朝着正确方向前进，而且正在带动整个市场。”

item.title: 大西洋月刊：斯蒂芬·米勒的政治思想是如何形成的
item.description:
在19世纪的法国，当中产阶级主要由保守、庸俗而自命不凡的人组成时，挑战他们的方式可能是写颓废诗歌，或者过一种违反传统道德规范的生活。 而在21世纪的圣莫尼卡，当中产阶级主要由自由派道德主义者组成时，挑衅他们就变成了公开炫耀那些按照自由派价值观本应让人感到羞愧的种族和阶级特权。 米勒从高中时期的煽动者，成长为主导美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）政策的人物，恰好反映了特朗普时代美国右翼政治的转变。 特朗普的政治风格，同样把幽默和怨愤混合在一起，与米勒从小收听的那些广播主持人如出一辙。 特朗普也承认彼此之间的这种联系。在第一个任期内，他向林博颁发了总统自由勋章。 但对许多“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）运动的追随者，尤其是年轻人来说，挑战自由派道德规范的游戏，已经演变成对自由民主制度的严重敌意。 过去，他们可能只是通过网络挑衅，或者以看到“自由派流泪”为乐。如今，这种态度已经转化为实实在在的政治敌视。 这种敌意的一个标志就是反犹太主义。无论在今天还是历史上的许多其他时期和地方，反犹太主义始终是极右翼政治的重要特征。 如今，这种情绪在极右翼内部如此流行，以至于共和党也无法将其彻底清除。 米勒似乎并不为此感到困扰。原因可能在于，他已经全心全意地认同自己的白人身份，并接受了白人是美国文明缔造者的观念。

item.title: Trump administration eyes tariff hikes on 16 trading partners after Supreme Court setback
item.description:
The Trump administration will propose new tariff hikes Tuesday night on the European Union, China, Mexico, Japan and 12 other trading partners, a major step towards recreating the president’s global duties the Supreme Court struck down in February.

According to one person with knowledge of the planning, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will announce the new tariff proposals as part of a report into the countries’ excess manufacturing capacity. The findings are the product of a trade investigation Greer’s office launched in March under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the U.S. trade representative to impose tariffs in response to unfair trade practices.

Three other people briefed by the administration on the investigation confirmed the report was in the process of being finalized and the results would be announced as soon as today. They were granted anonymity to share details of policy plans that are not yet public.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the announcement was coming.

The person with knowledge said the proposed new duties will honor the tariff ceilings countries have negotiated with the Trump administration over the past year, in exchange for trade concessions and massive investment in American industries. China’s overall tariff rate, for example, won’t exceed 20%, while the EU’s will stay below the 15% cap that the president agreed to with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Turnberry, Scotland in 2025.

Targeted countries will still have an opportunity to weigh in through hearings, public comments and closed-door talks for the rates are finalized. Like other recent tariff hikes, the new duties are also expected to come with a raft of carve-outs. And there will be an opportunity for future tariff reductions if countries take steps to reduce their manufacturing overcapacity, the person with knowlege said. But the threat of further tariffs, alone, is likely to enrage foreign allies already frustrated by other elements of Trump’s trade policies they believe violate their existing agreements.

In its filing in March, Greer’s office said there is evidence countries like China have aggressively expanded their production in strategic sectors beyond what demand can support and said the country, alongside other partners like the European Union, maintains a global goods surplus.

The investigation is the second of two sweeping trade probes launched in the spring as part of the Trump administration’s mission to rebuild its tariff regime after the "reciprocal" duties he imposed in 2025 were invalidated. The administration completed an investigation into forced labor in foreign supply chains over the summer, which it said justified tariffs of between 10 and 12.5 percent on dozens of trading partners, including all 16 of the economies covered by the excess manufacturing probe.

Any tariffs that are ultimately imposed following the excess manufacturing investigation would stack on top of those existing tariff rates.

Higher tariffs risks complicating delicate relationships with major economies and come amid a fragile trade truce with China that expires in January. Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are set to meet during the G20 summit next month.

It also comes amid tense negotiations with Mexico over the renewal of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement.

Like Trump’s other efforts to impose tariffs after his Supreme Court defeat, any new duties the government imposes based on this investigation are likely to be challenged in court. The administration’s forced labor tariffs are currently under scrutiny at the U.S. Court of International Trade.

Stefanie Bolzen contributed to this report.

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/24/trump-tariffs-china-eu-mexico-manufacturing-01181685

item.title: Democrats flip Tennessee's 4th District, giving the party 259 House seats
item.description:
Democrats' House majority grew to at least 259 seats on Tuesday — the party's largest since 1992 — after Victoria Broderick narrowly defeated Republican incumbent Scott DesJarlais in Tennessee's 4th Congressional District.

Broderick's victory comes two days after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th District. Foxx has held the seat since 2005.

The final balance of power in the Senate was settled on Nov. 17, when Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska gave Democrats their ninth flipped seat of the 2026 midterm elections, the most in nearly 70 years. When the next Congress takes office in early January, the party will hold its largest Senate majority since 2011, with 56 seats to the GOP's 44.

Though very few races remain unresolved, the dust has mostly settled on Democrats' 2026 landslide. Their sweeping victories in the U.S. House, Senate and statehouses nationwide add up to the biggest "blue wave" since Watergate.

The question now is what Democrats plan to do with their newfound power. Last week, the party nominated New York Rep. Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker, putting him on track to be the first Black American to wield the gavel. With a majority that could top out at 260 seats, Jeffries will have enormous leeway to send new legislation to the Senate while also blocking parts of President Trump's agenda, investigating his administration and possibly even impeaching him (again).

On the Senate side, Chuck Schumer of New York faces a challenge from Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen for majority leader. Senate Democrats will vote by secret ballot on Dec. 1, and the winner needs 28 votes. Schumer has 15 public backers to Van Hollen's five, with 34 senators undeclared, according to The Hill's count. Schumer says he has the votes. Van Hollen said Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press" that "we're north of 15 and momentum is in our direction."

Trump weighed in Sunday morning. "It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader," he wrote on Truth Social, two days after saying he could make deals with Schumer and Jeffries. Whoever wins will control which bills reach the floor, when votes occur and which judges and appointees are confirmed.

Among the priorities under discussion on both sides of the aisle: reinstating Affordable Care Act subsidies that expired under the previous Republican Congress; reversing nearly $1 trillion in recent GOP Medicaid cuts; expanding Medicare by lowering the eligibility age and adding vision, hearing and dental coverage; addressing the high prices of groceries and other goods by blocking Trump's global tariffs and restoring congressional power over trade policy; cutting off Iran war funding; and launching investigations of ICE, presidential pardons, political pressure on federal law enforcement, the Epstein files and the Trump family's business dealings. 

As for impeachment, Rep. Jamie Raskin, a Democrat from Maryland who is set to chair the House Judiciary Committee, told Punchbowl that it's a "critical tool in the constitutional toolbox" — but far from a sure thing. "We will not hesitate to use it if we think that the benefits exceed the costs," Raskin said. "But the one thing everybody's well aware of is that impeachment trials and impeachment motions soak up a lot of energy and oxygen."

Despite their sizable House and Senate majorities, Democrats will be limited in what legislation they can pass into law. Trump still has veto power, and Senate Republicans still hold enough seats to filibuster most bills. Meanwhile, many incoming Democratic lawmakers (like Peltola) are relative moderates representing red states and districts — meaning the party will have to calibrate its approach carefully to keep them on board and maximize its chances of winning the 2028 elections.

Beyond Washington, D.C., Democrats will now control the governorship and both legislative houses in six new states: Arizona, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Nevada, Michigan and Minnesota. They will also hold the majority in a dozen new statehouse chambers. As a result, the party will have more opportunities to experiment with new policy ideas, approve congressional maps, influence election procedures, fill Senate vacancies and help a new generation of governors build executive experience ahead of future presidential elections. 

It's even possible that state Democratic leaders could change the way we elect our next president by sidestepping the Electoral College and preventing candidates from winning the White House without winning the popular vote.

How many Senate seats did Democrats win?

Democrats came into the midterms needing a net gain of four seats to win back the Senate. To do that, they had to defend a handful of potentially vulnerable swing-state seats while also flipping at least a few seats in historically red states. 

That's exactly what happened. Republican efforts to flip blue seats in Michigan, Georgia, Minnesota and New Hampshire all came up well short. Meanwhile, Democrats won nine GOP-held seats in Mississippi, Maine, Texas, South Carolina, Ohio, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas and Alaska. 

Only two incumbent Republican senators in competitive races were able to win reelection: Florida's Ashley Moody and Nebraska's Pete Ricketts.

The last undecided race was called Nov. 17, as Mary Peltola defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan to become the first Alaska Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate since 2008.

Peltola secured just over 50% of the vote, narrowly clearing the threshold required to win without triggering Alaska's unique ranked choice voting system.

Democrats will enter 2027 with 56 seats in the Senate.

How many House seats did Democrats win?

So far, Democrats have won at least 258 U.S. House seats, far more than the 218 they needed for a majority. That includes 48 red-to-blue flips, for a net gain of 45 seats. That is four more than the 40 they picked up in Trump's first midterm in 2018. Democrats' 14-point victory in the House popular vote is the largest in any midterm since 1974.

Races that were too close to call on Election Night have been decided in the days that followed.

On Sunday, the AP called North Carolina's 5th District for Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist, over Rep. Virginia Foxx, who has held the seat since 2005. Cook Political Report had rated the seat likely Republican, and Foxx won it by nearly 19 points in 2024. Foxx, who requested a recount last week, said in a statement that she had called Hubbard to congratulate him. She has already filed to run for the seat again in 2028, WFMY reported.

Democrats picked up another flip on Tuesday when Broderick was named the winner in Tennessee's 4th District, defeating DesJarlais by just a few hundred votes. Broderick will be the lone Democrat among the Volunteer State's House caucus.

Where things stand in the undecided House races

Three U.S. House races remain unresolved.

Two are in Louisiana, where the top two finishers in the 5th and 6th Districts will meet in a Dec. 12 runoff.

The last remaining House race that will be decided based on votes cast on Election Day is in Minnesota's 1st District, where Democrat Jake Johnson leads GOP Rep. Brad Finstad by just over 300 votes. Finstad requested a recount, which runs Nov. 30 to Dec. 3. The state canvassing board will certify the race Dec. 8.

How many governorships did Democrats win?

Republican governors have outnumbered their Democratic counterparts for the last 15 years straight (and for 26 of the last 30 years overall). But this year, Democrats have reversed the "governor gap," flipping six governorships in Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Alaska and Georgia to bring their total to 30 — the party's first gubernatorial majority since 2011.

On Thursday, Democrats also held onto Kansas, where voters elected Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher to become the Sunflower State's fourth woman governor ever. She defeated Republican Ty Masterson, the state's Senate president.

"Kansans have sent a clear message that they want to keep our state moving forward," Holscher said in a video posted online Tuesday. "The work of preparing to lead has already begun."

The AP called Alaska's governor race for Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins early Saturday. He won a majority of first-choice votes, so no ranked-choice count was needed. He will be the state's first Democratic governor since Tony Knowles left office in 2002, and he takes office Dec. 7.

How many state legislatures did Democrats win? 

Democrats' gains were also seen at the state level. They flipped more than 500 state legislative seats across the country and turned a total of 12 legislative chambers blue.

That includes three states where they flipped both chambers: Arizona, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. After Election Day's results, Democrats will control the House, Senate and governorship in Arizona for the first time since 1966. Democrats also secured a "trifecta" in Wisconsin. They'll hold both legislative chambers in New Hampshire, but the governorship in the Granite State will remain in Republican hands. 

Democrats regained trifectas in Minnesota, Michigan and Pennsylvania by clinching majorities in the lone GOP-led chamber in their states. They flipped a single chamber in Georgia, North Carolina and Texas, ensuring that Democratic governors in those states won't face unified Republican opposition within their state legislatures. 

Where things stand in the undecided state legislative races

As of Monday morning, only three state legislative chambers — the North Carolina Senate and both chambers in Alaska — remained undecided, according to the AP. A recount is possible in North Carolina, where Senate control hinges on one race.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/article/final-2026-midterm-election-results-democrats-reach-258-house-seats-their-most-since-1992-as-foxx-concedes-in-north-carolina-what-they-can-and-cant-do-next-182515399.html

item.title: Al Gore returns to his roots with plan to buy his 113-year-old hometown newspaper
item.description:
Al Gore is getting back into the newspaper business after starting his career as an Army journalist.

But this time, he’s buying the paper.

The former vice president is set to buy the Carthage Courier, his hometown paper in Tennessee, from the family of Hershel and Geraldine Lake, the Courier announced this week. The sale — which is expected to close in the coming weeks — would end the family’s 50-year run at the 113-year-old paper.

“When my hometown paper came up for sale, I saw an opportunity to help preserve the Courier as an independent voice for Carthage and Smith County,” Gore said in a statement.

The Courier, a weekly newspaper, said it will keep publishing through the transition and retain all of its staff.

Before he ran for Congress in 1976, Gore spent six months as an Army journalist and worked as an investigative reporter for The Tennessean in Nashville. He went on to represent Tennessee in both chambers of Congress, before serving eight years as Bill Clinton’s vice president.

Gore won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007 alongside the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and currently resides on his farm in Carthage.

“I look forward to supporting the Carthage Courier team, many of whom have served this community for decades, as they continue to provide vital information and serve this community for generations to come,” Gore said.

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/24/al-gore-newspaper-carthage-courier-01182203

item.title: 观点：大胜的民主党能不能把握住机会，将是个严峻的考验
item.description:
文章认为，民主党在2026年中期选举中取得远超预期的胜利，不仅拿下众议院，还以56席控制参议院，并在多个州赢得关键职位。作者将其视为选民要求政治变革的“蓝色海啸”。 民主党进步派及部分选民要求更换哈基姆·杰弗里斯和查克·舒默，批评两人在以色列政策、移民、企业捐款和全民医保等议题上未能回应民意。文章援引民调称，多数民主党选民支持更换舒默。 杰弗里斯最终以251票赞成、11票反对、2票弃权当选党内领袖，七名新议员公开表示投下反对票。马里兰州参议员克里斯·范霍伦则正式挑战舒默，并主张民主党竞选机构不应接受AIPAC资金。 作者认为，民主党只有两年时间证明自己能否兑现选民对全民医保、富人增税、堕胎权、移民改革等议题的期待；若领导层继续维持现状，这次选举胜利可能难以转化为长期多数。

item.title: Thanksgiving travelers are bracing for delays after a wave of airline tech outages
item.description:
The timing couldn't have been worse. Just before the busiest travel week of the year, a wave of major aviation tech outages — including a Delta Air Lines system failure on Sunday, a United Airlines disruption last Monday and a nationwide FAA ground stop on Nov. 13 — looked sure to make leaving home for Thanksgiving more stressful than ever. 

Suddenly, "outage anxiety" was everywhere. "I think half the country is looking at its boarding pass with suspicion," Christopher Elliott, founder of a nonprofit that helps consumers resolve travel disputes, told the New York Times.

According to a YouGov poll conducted right after the ground stop, nearly three-quarters of Americans (72%) said that if they were set to fly over the holiday, they would be concerned about experiencing "flight cancellations or significant delays as a result of further disruptions to U.S. air travel." And nearly a third (31%) said the ground stop could potentially alter their plans, making them less likely to travel by air for Thanksgiving.

AAA projects nearly 6 million people will fly domestically over the seven-day Thanksgiving travel period.

But now that the digital chaos seems to have subsided and Americans are starting to hit the road, how worried should you really be about additional meltdowns snarling your holiday travel plans?

The simple answer: We don't know. 

An outage is, by definition, unexpected. The FAA said it was forced to ground thousands of flights after a router installed during a copper-to-fiber network upgrade flooded its telecommunications network with excessive data, overwhelming legacy equipment and destabilizing radar and communications feeds. Delta's outage was traced to a "database issue" in its automated weight-and-balance system. United's outage was similar. None were the result of a cyberattack, officials insisted. But none were foreseen, either. 

"This has never happened," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CBS News, referring to the chain of events that triggered the ground stop. "And so that's why … we felt comfortable doing [the upgrade] in the middle of the day — because it's been done thousands of times. We've never had this situation." 

On Nov. 16, the Trump administration convened a "tiger team" — a small group of experts or specialists who work together on solving a specific problem that isn't easily addressed by normal operations — to prevent similar outages going forward. Composed of officials from the FAA, the Transportation Department, the Defense Department and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the team has "met every day this week to ensure continuity of service," according to the Daily Wire.

A White House spokesperson said Americans preparing to travel for Thanksgiving have nothing to worry about, the outlet added.

"President Trump and Secretary Duffy have brought together the best and the brightest across the government to ensure what happened [on Nov. 13] can never happen again," the spokesperson said. "Work continues, and Americans can rest assured their country's aviation is the best in the world."

Why tech upgrades can cause outages

But even if travelers survive the Thanksgiving rush without major incident, the experts suggest that future outages are simply inevitable. 

According to Microsoft President and Vice Chair Brad Smith — whose own company suffered a massive global outage earlier this month — AI is the common thread here, even if it didn't directly cause any of the recent travel disruptions. 

"What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you're a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems," he told CBS News on Sunday. 

Smith went on to say that organizations are now rushing to patch vulnerabilities "at a pace we have never seen before" —a rush that itself creates instability, particularly within legacy systems. 

"Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you're trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can't take as much time to test what you're changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong," he explained.

The bottom line? Americans "have to be prepared" for more disruptions in "the coming months because this isn't the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks," Smith said. "The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now."

Even as the White House tries to reassure Thanksgiving travelers, administration officials have predicted that more outages are on the way. 

"The American people should understand that a great deal of our digital infrastructure is dated. It is old. It has been built out over three decades or more. We are in a period of technological step change, both in terms of what people refer to as [AI] models, applications, and the like, and in computing power," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN on Sunday.

"And in that technological step change, our systems are going to need to be upgraded," Clayton continued. "They're going to need to be upgraded for performance and for cybersecurity. And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service. That is going to happen."

Asked if "the American people" should "just be prepared for more outages" because of those upgrades, Clayton effectively said yes.

"They should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said. "Any time you refurbish your house, upgrade any of your systems, there are going to be things that you do not expect." 

How to prepare

With that in mind, it's probably wise to plan for the worst if you're leaving home for the holiday — especially if you're flying. Print everything: boarding passes, visas and so on. Forgo checked bags, if possible. (Or at least track your luggage.) Keep your receipts. And know your rights: Transportation Department rules require airlines to issue a refund if your flight is canceled or significantly delayed for any reason (assuming you decline a replacement ticket or travel credit).

After all, outages aren’t the only obstacle to consider this weekend. Major storms are also set to strike both coasts — including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day — and record-challenging king tides are threatening coastal flooding from California to Florida as a result of El Niño.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo Travel at https://travel.yahoo.com/flights/article/aviation-tech-outages-thanksgiving-travel-205820796.html

item.title: 华人大V观选 “选举证明两岸互不隶属”
item.description:
来源: 
自由亚洲

时事评论员公子沈（左）及资深媒体人李肃（右）接受自由亚洲电台采访，分享他们对台湾2026年九合一选举的看法。 (RFA拍摄及制图)

“不管是谁当选，都是证明台湾人民有自己的独立主权，能够自由地选择自己的中意的候选人......再次用实际行动证明中华民国和中华人民共和国互不隶属。”

来自加拿大的华文自媒体工作者“公子沈”周二（24日）接受了自由亚洲电台的专访。台湾九合一地方选举将于11月28日投票，多位活跃网路舆论的独立评论人、媒体工作者受邀到台湾观选。

华人大V观选  "选举证明两岸互不隶属”

除了公子沈外，曾任美国之音记者的李肃，也在观选团之列。在受访前，他已经走访了台东、台南、宜兰等地。李肃说，在台东街头更多看到的是助选车辆，沿街拜票只遇到一次。但在台北，他才感觉到这场选举的热度，主因当然也是民进党籍台北市长候选人沈伯洋掀起的「洋流」。

李肃说，自己早就因为黑熊学院和民防议题知道沈伯洋，但“从来没有想象过他会来竞争台北市长”。他认为，蒋万安有现任市长的知名度，沈伯洋则在选战中凭具体的民生议题获得更多关注。

李肃判断，北京可能更在意这场选举会如何影响台湾政坛未来走向，因为台北市长选战能让政治人物获得全国关注，也可能影响2028年总统选举前的政治布局。

“我相信大陆也看得很清楚，沈伯洋对于大陆的看法，大概是看得比较透一些”，李肃说。“所以他们（大陆）担心的是说沈伯洋如果上来，他对于台湾整个的走向，会坚持台湾对抗的路，而不会走什么一国两制、和平共处。”

公子沈认为，沈伯洋这样一个被贴上“台独分子”标签，被中共通缉和制裁的人，如今成为了炙手可热的一个政治明星。 这样的情况，反映出的不只是台北市市政的问题，而是整个台湾的民主能不能维持，或者说台湾人的政治权利是不是受到中共影响，被渗透的问题。 沈伯洋的异军突起，对公子沈而言，不只是台湾实践了民主，更有主权是独立于中华人民共和国的意义。

至于争取连任的国民党籍现任市长蒋万安。公子沈说，他印象最深的就是他是蒋经国的孙子 —- 虽然这一点仍然争议 — 但这仍是蒋最鲜明的标签，也是亮点，能够吸引大量的国民党的支持者。再者，蒋万安曾经在美国留学，然后长得也算不错，形象比较好。公子沈认为，这是一位清新、年轻，又有国民党背景的明星政治人物。“蒋”这个姓对他也是一个巨大的加分。

感受台湾民众对选举的热情

公子沈来自加拿大，被问道他认为台湾和加拿大的选举有什么不同。他回忆，之前在加拿大参加一场地方竞选活动时，市长和市议员候选人在图书馆摆桌，与来访居民交谈。在台北，他看到竞选团队把政见做成展览，也看到下班民众排队领取竞选刊物。他说，这些做法让他感受到台湾民众对选举的热情。他认为，台湾经历过戒严，今天民众愿意花时间了解候选人、公开表达支持，也反映出他们对手中选票的重视。

“可能也因为台湾民主是比较新的民主，只有几十年的历程，而且过去曾经有过这样一个比较艰辛的戒严时期，很多人受到迫害，所以大家对自己手上的选票比较重视，会想办法去把选举体现出来，真正体现出人民的意志来，而且变成花样去体现，所以这一点是其他国家所没有的，我也是对台湾的选举文化还有选举热情很感动的地方”，公子沈说。

谈到其他民主社会可以从台湾观察什么，公子沈以加拿大作比较。他认为，北京在加拿大施加影响力时，较集中于部分华人选区和社群。在台湾，语言相通，加上两岸经贸和社会联系，网络信息操作可以触及更广的受众。对他而言，这场选举提出了一个其他民主社会也会遇到的问题：选民如何在外部压力和真假难辨的信息中，仍能按照自己的判断投票。

中共介选，台、加型态有别

对于中共介选议题，李肃从选举层级看北京可能介入的程度。他认为，九合一选举主要涉及地方治理，北京整体的介入力度可能低于总统选举，但台北仍值得关注。他说，首都市长选战具有全国性的政治影响，可能牵动2028年总统选举前的布局。依他的判断，北京关注沈伯洋，除了看这次台北市长选战，也在看他日后是否可能在台湾政坛扮演更重要的角色。

公子沈则比较了中共在加拿大和台湾的介选作为。他说， 中共对加拿大的介入跟台湾的介入还是有很大差别的，特别在规模上。中共在台湾介选的规模非常大，因为文化相近，经济影响力也比较大。从政府到立法院，再到商业团体、民间团体，乃至普通人获取资讯的渠道，全方位的渗透和认知战。

但在加拿大，中共会“精选“介入的对象，挑华人选区的某些议员进行收买和渗透，包括华人社群的一些统战组织。“因为它（中共）是定点打击，所以我们就可以定点摘除“。公子沈说，现在加拿大的社会，包括情报部门、民间的人士都对中共盯得很紧。“而在台湾我看到的是，他们（中共）好像肆无忌惮。"

关键词: 
台湾地方选举
两岸关系
栏目: 
时事见解
作者: 
Alan Lu
温珒仪
吴晓

item.title: 国际刑事法院遭美国制裁面临瘫痪 日籍院长求助高市
item.description:
来源: 
法新社

国际刑事法院（ICC）10月遭美国广泛制裁，财务及运作面临瘫痪威胁。日籍院长赤根智子今天拜会日本首相高市早苗后，日本政府宣布将提前在今年内缴清明年应缴分摊费用。

日本外务省发布声明表示，日本是国际刑事法院最大出资国，为了予以支持，决定提前缴清分摊费用。

据日本媒体报导，日本通常最早在每年4月缴纳当年分摊款。

日本外务省的声明还说，高市今天告诉赤根，日本政府将“继续大力支持国际刑事法院及赤根院长，让法院得以发挥原本设想的角色与功能”。

赤根则在与高市会面后对媒体记者表示，国际刑事法院将以明智方式运用其经费，以确保维持运作及员工薪资和其他费用获得支付。

关键词: 
国际刑事法院
日本
高市早苗

item.title: Thomas Markle indicted in Los Angeles over alleged child sexual abuse material
item.description:
Meghan Markle’s father, Thomas Markle Sr., has been indicted on child pornography charges in California, just days after a Florida judge determined that he is mentally fit to stand trial.

Thomas Sr., 82, has been charged with two counts of possession of child pornography and faces up to 40 years in prison if convicted.

The indictment was shared on X by Bill Essayli, the United States Attorney for the Central District of California, who noted that Thomas Sr. stands accused of “knowingly” possessing “35mm film negatives of sexually explicit material involving children.”

“Federal law enforcement was notified last month that Markle possessed child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in the Philippines and at two storage units in Los Angeles,” Essayli continued in his statement. “A judicially approved search warrant was executed and the materials were seized.”

The indictment refers to several specific frames that were uncovered by the FBI and that contain “at least one image of child pornography [that] involved a prepubescent minor and a minor who had not attained 12 years of age.”

Thomas Sr., who is currently being detained in Florida, “is expected to be arraigned on the indictment in the coming weeks in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles,” Essayli continued.

“This is an ongoing investigation. Markle is presumed innocent until proven guilty,” he concluded, while asking anyone with any knowledge of those involved with child pornography materials to contact the FBI.

It comes after a judge in Florida ruled that the former director of photography is able to stand trial, following a competency review by a psychiatrist, who found that Thomas Sr. — who was diagnosed with dementia earlier this year — has “sufficient ability to understand the nature and consequences of the charges against him.”

Thomas Sr. was supported at the Tampa courthouse by his daughter, Samantha Markle, and her partner, Mark Phillips, who told Page Six that the couple was doing “not too bad.”

Samantha, meanwhile, told reporters her dad was “doing great, thanks.”

Thomas Sr. was set to have a preliminary hearing in Florida on Dec. 1, but now that he’s been indicted in the Golden State — where investigators discovered alleged child abuse materials in a storage locker registered to his name — his case will now be heard in California.

Thomas Sr. was arrested in Florida at the Maravida Senior Living care home on Nov. 6 on federal charges of child porn possession.

He was taken into custody after FBI agents found material suspected of containing child sexual abuse imagery in multiple Los Angeles-area storage units that were registered to Thomas Sr.

Thomas Sr. — who has been in a wheelchair since his left leg was amputated last December — was initially released on bond back to his care home, but he was detained just days later after cutting off his ankle monitor in the middle of the night.

Following his Florida arrest, Thomas was hit with child abuse charges in the Philippines after finding himself under investigation by the Cebu City Police Office. 

His son, Thomas Markle Jr., allegedly discovered child sexual abuse materials in his father’s home and storage unit in the Philippines, and reported the alleged findings to the police.

Daily Mail reporters also allegedly discovered similar materials in Thomas Sr.’s abandoned storage near his former home in Rosarito, Mexico.

Thomas Sr. denied his son’s allegations, telling the Daily Mail in October that he paid for sex in the Philippines but did not sleep with underage girls.

Samantha, meanwhile, accused Thomas Jr. of a “revenge” scheme and vehemently defended her father.

As for Meghan, she said in a statement to Page Six that she was “deeply distressed” by her half-brother’s allegations against her estranged father.

The Duchess of Sussex’s mom, Doria Ragland, reportedly helped the FBI identify her ex in disturbing child sex abuse photos.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call the Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-330-0226.

This article originally appeared on Page Six at https://pagesix.com/2026/11/24/celebrity-news/meghan-markles-dad-thomas-indicted-on-child-porn-charges-in-california-faces-40-years-in-prison/?utm_source=yahoo&utm_campaign=pagesix&utm_medium=referral

item.title: CIA and intel director’s office reportedly hit by hack affecting unclassified information
item.description:
The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence suffered an apparent hack affecting unclassified information, four sources familiar with the matter told CNN.

The intrusion hit a system the agencies draw on​ for open-source intelligence analysis, one of the sources said.

The full extent of the breach was unclear, but officials emphasized that no classified information was affected. “There have been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems,” an ODNI official told CNN.

The CIA declined to comment.

It is not immediately clear when the hack occurred, who was responsible for it, or if it has been resolved.

The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), which oversees 17 US intelligence agencies, including the CIA, has in recent years invested in open-source intelligence work, which is often unclassified.

The apparent intrusion, which the New York Times first reported, is the latest in a string of cybersecurity incidents or tech outages that have rattled the US government and private sector.

The incident does not appear to be related to an apparent hack of the FBI’s nationwide criminal information database, two of the sources said, which CNN first reported on Friday.

The hacking incidents have coincided with a series of unrelated high-profile tech outages affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the FAA’s air traffic control system that have rattled Americans’ confidence in the technology that underpins their lives.

All flights nationwide were grounded for hours earlier this month after a massive systems failure, leading to thousands of flights being delayed or canceled. The Federal Aviation Administration traced the problem to a single router in Arkansas.

Separately, an outage affecting Microsoft products left people around the world unable to access staples of work life like Outlook email accounts and Teams meetings.

But it’s the disruption at the NSA, the US’ signals intelligence spy agency, and intrusions at the FBI and CIA that have national security officials on alert.

The highly classified network that the NSA uses for its internal communications went down for multiple days last week, CNN first reported. The apparent cause was a software update gone wrong and not a cyberattack, the nation’s spy chief Jay Clayton said. A critical Georgia facility that supports signals intelligence and cybersecurity operations focused on the Middle East, where the US is currently engaged in a war with Iran was also impacted, CNN reported.

The NSA’s most sensitive and important intelligence-gathering systems were unaffected by the outage, and by Friday, the outage was resolved.

The software vulnerabilities that the NSA was addressing are just a handful in a slew of new vulnerabilities that artificial intelligence has been able to locate. Cybersecurity experts say government agencies and companies alike are discovering a spate of new software bugs in their systems thanks to AI, prompting a rush to fix them and sometimes mistakes along the way.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

This article originally appeared on CNN at https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/24/politics/cia-odni-hack-unclassified-information

item.title: 印尼扣留中国运出的405吨导弹氧化剂
item.description:
来源: 
新唐人

印度尼西亚海军宣布扣留一艘中国始发的货轮，船上载有405吨高氯酸钠，可以制造100枚导弹。网民纷纷猜测，这些货物到底是给谁的？

印尼海军11月20日在记者会上宣布，11月7日在北苏门答腊勿拉湾（Belawan）附近拦截科摩罗籍货船Star Line，查获405吨高氯酸钠。军方称，高氯酸钠本身不能燃烧，但可以作为燃料的氧化剂，用来制造导弹推进剂或者爆炸物。这405吨高氯酸钠如果用来制造导弹，可以制造100枚。

船上还设有一个化学混合槽，让人怀疑这批货物可能是为了进行进一步加工，而非单纯为了商业转售而运输。

此外，船上也载有数百万张空白未注册的4G SIM卡，与大量军民两用战略化学品同时装载，引发外界对预定收货人及货物用途的质疑。

据报该船原名Anjie Sun，隶属中国船东。今年5月卖出并改名Star Line，换挂科摩罗（Comoros）国旗。印尼海军扣查船上文件发现，该船注册状态已被暂停，船东登记在阿联酋，船舶管理记录中也列有一家香港公司。

这艘船9月12日从中国连云港出发，AIS系统设定的下一站目的地为孟加拉第二大港蒙古拉港（Mongla Port），原定11月8日抵达。

目前不清楚这艘船为什么在海上漂流两个月才抵达印尼。从中国出发前往孟加拉，只需穿行马六甲海峡，本不应该行经印尼。

印尼海军表示，11月7日这艘船在勿拉湾外海进行计划外的加油停靠。海军发现该船行为异常，并拒绝应答，于是将其扣留盘查。

该船标注的目的地是孟加拉，但是孟加拉两个港口的海关都表示，没有接到过这艘船的舱单。另外，孟加拉是一个小国，平均每年才进口数十公斤的高氯酸钠。这一船的数量等于该国一万年的进口总量。

印尼官方没有公布这艘船的货主及最终目的地。网民纷纷猜测到底是运往何方。

许多华人网民认为，该船目的地可能是伊朗等少数几个中东国家。有网民留言：“感觉是去伊朗的。”另一个网友回应：“把‘感觉’两字去掉。”

还有网民说：“全世界没有几个国家能生产 sim 卡，但是只有个别几个国家，既不能生产 sim 卡，也不能光明正大从国际上买 sim 的。”

有人猜测这些SIM卡的目的地可能是迪拜的电诈园区，也有人认为可能是给伊朗制造无人机。

关键词: 
印尼
中国货轮
高氯酸钠
栏目: 
要闻
作者: 
历澄宇

item.title: 81.5 million Americans expected to travel as Thanksgiving storms threaten both coasts
item.description:
Millions of Americans hitting the road and skies for Thanksgiving could run into storms on both coasts, including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day. Record-challenging king tides are forecast on both coasts, threatening coastal flooding from California to Florida.

"A strong coastal storm will bring heavy rain, strong winds, and instances of coastal flooding for much of the East Coast during Thanksgiving," according to a Tuesday afternoon update from the National Weather Service Prediction Center. The coastal storm could also bring winter precipitation in the Mid-Mississippi Valley.

On the West Coast, king tides combined with a bombardment of Pacific storm systems could cause flooding on low-lying California coastal roads and increase beach erosion through Thanksgiving.

Weather hasn't been the only problem facing travelers. Delta Air Lines resolved an outage that caused delays nationwide Sunday, marking the third major disruption to U.S. air travel in nine days.

AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million by car and 5.96 million on domestic flights.

Tuesday and Wednesday: Atmospheric river in the West, storms in the Southeast

In the Pacific Northwest and Northern California, a barrage of storm systems will bring rain and wintry precipitation to higher elevations on Tuesday, then move into Washington and Oregon on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the NWS.

"Near the coast, there are Marginal Risks (level 1 of 4) of excessive rainfall today in Northern California, and on Wednesday and Thursday through portions of the coastal Pacific Northwest," the NWS said Tuesday.

According to AccuWeather meteorologist Alyssa Glenny, "People heading to the coast for Thanksgiving should check high tide times and local road conditions. Storm-driven increases in water levels and wave action can make flooding worse when they overlap with high tide."

Glenny also said that coastal flooding can happen even when it's not raining. In other words: sunshine doesn't necessarily mean the roads will be dry.

In the San Francisco Bay Area, the storms coincide with potentially record-breaking king tides, the year's highest tides. The National Weather Service has a coastal flood warning in effect until 4 p.m. PT Thursday and calls Tuesday and Wednesday an "extreme" risk for flooding along the bay shoreline, and a high surf warning covers Wednesday on the Pacific coast. The agency said the storm will coincide with the king tides, potentially making flooding worse during Thanksgiving travel.

San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie wrote in a Tuesday X post, "On Wednesday, 11/25, we are expecting high tides and big swells around 11 am so stay away from Ocean Beach and the waterfront. Look out for each other, stay alert, and don't drive through floodwaters."

In Marin County, Southern Marin Fire District has urged residents and businesses to "take action now" and prepare for possible road closures and travel disruptions.

Further north, in Humboldt County, Sheriff William Honsal declared a local emergency and ordered residents of the King Salmon area on Humboldt Bay to leave by 7 a.m. Tuesday, after seawater flooded streets there during Monday's high tide, according to the sheriff's office.

In the Southeast, heavy rain and thunderstorms could hit Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. AccuWeather said Wednesday could bring some of the most widespread weather-related travel disruptions before Thanksgiving, particularly in the Southeast, with airline delays expected to expand in Orlando and Miami from Tuesday to Wednesday and in Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday. The National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center has warned of flooding rain along the coastal Carolinas on Wednesday. Delays at those hubs could ripple across the country.

Thanksgiving Day: Possible major storm in the Northeast

Forecasters are monitoring another storm that will form off the Southeast coast late Wednesday and move up the East Coast through Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain and strong winds from the Mid-Atlantic to New England.

"Significant coastal flooding and beach erosion are the primary concerns from Georgia to the Northeast, especially on Wednesday and Thursday; driven by strong onshore winds, high surf, and astronomical tides," according to the NWS.

"The greatest impacts and flooding potential are expected along the Mid-Atlantic coast from the northern Outer Banks to New Jersey. Heavy rainfall is expected from the Southeast on Northward through southern New England."

The National Weather Service in Boston called it a "potentially significant coastal storm" for Thanksgiving into Friday, with gusts along the coast possibly topping 50 mph. Very high tides could also bring coastal flooding, the agency said. The storm arrives as king tides continue on both coasts around Tuesday's full moon, which could worsen coastal flooding, the Weather Channel said.

Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. AccuWeather said a brief period of wet snow or sleet is possible in northern New York and New England later Thursday.

That could be a problem for the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which is set to start at 8:30 a.m. Thursday. The parade's giant balloons can't fly if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph, Fox Weather reported. Rain is forecast to begin around midday, possibly before the parade ends, with conditions deteriorating significantly in the afternoon, AccuWeather reported.

The weekend after Thanksgiving

The National Weather Service expects the East Coast storm to weaken and move away, though windy conditions and some rain or snow showers could linger in parts of New England and the eastern Great Lakes into the weekend.

Another storm could form in the East during the busy return weekend, while more Pacific storms could hit the West Coast. The Sunday after Thanksgiving is typically one of the busiest travel days of the year.

Washington State Ferries has canceled several sailings because of high tides from Tuesday into the weekend, with about 300,000 people expected to use the ferry system over the holiday period.

Forecasters advise travelers to check forecasts for both their departure and arrival cities, and to keep an eye on flight status before heading to the airport.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/weather-news/article/thanksgiving-travel-and-weather-forecast-storms-on-both-coasts-could-snarl-busiest-travel-days-san-francisco-braces-for-potentially-record-king-tides-222342659.html

item.title: 前年被李显龙点名“接班人” 陈吉宁吓坏掩盖消息
item.description:
来源: 
新唐人

2024年11月28日，新加坡国务资政李显龙（左）在上海会见中共上海市委书记陈吉宁。（中共上海市政府外事办公室）

中共上海市委书记陈吉宁突然被官宣落马，舆论猜测可能与党魁习近平消除政治威胁有关。2024年新加坡前总理李显龙访问上海后曾提到中共“下一代领导人”，据报陈吉宁被吓坏。

北京时间11月24日晚，中共党媒突然宣布中共政治局委员、上海市委书记陈吉宁落马，震惊海内外。多名学者分析，习近平可能想打掉潜在“接班人”。

最近两年来，多家外媒盘点所谓习近平“接班人”，都曾点名分析陈吉宁继任的可能性。分析人士指出，习近平想长期掌权，被外媒点名“接班”可能成为这名官员的“催命符”。

今年9月，《日经亚洲》文章分析新任上海市长朱忠明“接班”可能性时，也曾提及上海书记陈吉宁。

文章提到，2024年11月，新加坡国务资政、前总理李显龙访问上海，会见了陈吉宁。李显龙回国后受访时称，他对陈吉宁印象深刻，并称“我也希望与中国（中共）下一代领导人们建立新的联系”。因为李显龙会晤陈吉宁之前，刚刚在北京见过习近平，当时外界热议李显龙是不是已经得知中共人事布局。

文章说，这场“接班”猜测对陈吉宁而言，恐怕并非好事。只要外界认为他有意取代习近平，即使只是些微的政治野心，都可能招致习近平不满，断送政治前途。据知情人士透露，当时陈吉宁及其身边人士极力阻止相关消息在中国境内扩散，以免升温成为中共党内议题。

文章分析指，习可能计划掌权至2032年以后，“60后”官员“接班”的可能性不高。

翻查2024年新加坡媒体放出的新闻视频（链接）可见，当李显龙说出“我也希望与中国（中共）下一代领导人们建立新的联系”时，画面中出现的是他和陈吉宁握手的画面。当时这些报导曾引发舆论高度关注。

实际上，类似的戏码也曾在重庆市上演。2019年，时任新加坡副总理兼财政部长王瑞杰访问重庆，与时任中共重庆市委书记陈敏儿对话。王瑞杰当时直言，希望此次会议能为“我们（两国）下一代领导人铺路”。

当时王瑞杰被认为是新加坡总理继任人选。因此外界分析，这番话摆明了是将陈敏儿视为“习近平的接班人”。

陈敏儿随后被平调到地位不如重庆的天津市，没能升任中共政治局常委，明显已被习近平边缘化。

关键词: 
李显龙
接班人
陈吉宁
习近平

要闻
作者: 
历澄宇

item.title: Chinese tech giant convicted in sweeping U.S. criminal case over its business in Iran
item.description:
By Karen Freifeld

NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came ‌in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access ‌to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions ​violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027.

Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei's activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial.

"After the media started questioning Huawei's operations in ‌Iran, so did Huawei's banks," prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during ⁠closing arguments in the case last week.

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its "good-faith compliance culture."

"We fully expect to appeal," Heberlig told reporters.

US Attorney Joseph Nocella said in a ⁠statement: “Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the enforcement of US laws.” China's embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make ​a ​significant difference.

Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei's business, as the company diversified and emerged ​as a key player in China's push for artificial intelligence.

FOUNDER'S DAUGHTER ‌WAS DETAINED

In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and daughter of the company's founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei's business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero's welcome. The charges against her were dropped.

Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled ‌HSBC, Standard Chartered and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges ​in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.

THE ​PROSECUTION CASE

During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from ​Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel's antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by ‌semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei ​employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile ​testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu booth at a trade show to photograph a device.

Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng's deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran.

The defense argued that HSBC and the other banks ​knew about Huawei's business in Iran and were competing for ‌Huawei's business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having "cherry-picked" a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said ​Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development."

The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries.

(Additional reporting ​by Luc Cohen and Jonathan Stempel; Editing by Jonathan Spicer, Noeleen Walder and Will Dunham)

This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/chinas-huawei-convicted-us-criminal-201624138.html

item.title: 上海市委书记陈吉宁被调查
item.description:
储百亮
2026年11月25日

The Communist Party leader of Shanghai, Chen Jining, has been placed under investigation on suspicion of “serious violations,” the Chinese government announced on Tuesday. It was a stunning downfall for an official who had widely been seen as destined for a higher role under the country’s top leader, Xi Jinping.

中国政府周二宣布，上海市委书记陈吉宁因涉嫌“严重违纪违法”正接受调查。作为一位普遍被视为将在中国最高领导人习近平治下晋升更高职位的官员，他的落马令人震惊。

The investigation into Mr. Chen was announced in a brief bulletin from Xinhua, China’s official news agency, which gave no details about reasons. The bulletin said that Mr. Chen was suspected of “serious violations of discipline and the law,” a phrase that usually refers to allegations of corruption.

对陈吉宁的调查是通过中国官方通讯社新华社的一则简短通报宣布的，通报未给出具体原因。通报称，陈吉宁涉嫌“严重违纪违法”，这一表述通常指涉腐败指控。

Mr. Chen, 62, an environmental scientist trained in Britain, rose as a university president and minister for environmental protection. He went on to become mayor of Beijing and, from 2022, party secretary of Shanghai — a key post in charge of one of China’s most important commercial cities that often opens the way to central leadership.

现年62岁的陈吉宁是一名曾在英国深造的环境科学家，历任大学校长和环保部部长。此后他出任北京市市长，并于2022年起担任上海市委书记——这一关键职位掌管着中国最重要的商业城市之一，往往意味着仕途将通往中央领导层。

His abrupt treatment suggests that Mr. Xi’s expanding drive against corruption and disloyalty means that even seemingly secure protégés cannot feel safe as Mr. Xi prepares to claim an all-but-certain fourth term ruling China. Other officials made subject to investigations have gone on to face prosecution, conviction and imprisonment.

对他的突然处置表明，随着习近平准备开启几乎毫无悬念的第四个执政任期，在其不断扩大的反腐与整肃不忠行动之下，即便是看似稳固的亲信也无法高枕无忧。以往接受调查的官员随后会面临起诉、定罪和监禁。

One month ago, Mr. Xi presided over a meeting of the Communist Party Central Committee where he called for a renewed campaign for discipline and loyalty. The meeting also announced preparations for a party congress next year, at which Mr. Xi is almost certain to win another five years as general secretary.

一个月前，习近平主持召开了一次中共中央委员会会议，他在会上呼吁开展新一轮纪律和忠诚整顿行动。会议还宣布筹备明年的党代会，习近平几乎肯定将在会上再次获得五年的总书记任期。

Many analysts thought that Mr. Chen could rise to become premier, or at least a vice premier, in Mr. Xi’s next administration. Mr. Chen had won a reputation as a technocrat whose scientific education blended well with Mr. Xi’s technological priorities.

许多分析人士曾认为，陈吉宁有望在习近平的下一届政府中晋升为总理，或至少担任副总理。陈吉宁一直被视为技术官僚，其科学教育背景与习近平的科技优先事项十分契合。

Mr. Chen is also a member of the party’s Politburo, a council of leading central and local officials. He is now virtually certain to be expelled from the party and from the Politburo, which would mean that four of the 24 Politburo members elected in 2022 had been removed and investigated. One of those was Zhang Youxia, China’s topmost general until his removal this year.

陈吉宁同时也是中共中央政治局委员，该机构由中央和地方主要领导官员组成。如今他几乎肯定将被开除党籍并被免去政治局委员职务，这意味着2022年选出的24名政治局委员中，已有四人被免职和接受调查。其中包括今年被免职前一直是中国军队最高将领的张又侠。

This month, Mr. Chen convened a meeting in Shanghai where he warned officials to abide by Mr. Xi’s warnings against corruption and other abuses of power.

本月，陈吉宁在上海主持召开了一次会议，他在会上告诫官员要遵守习近平关于反腐败及其他滥用权力行为的警示。

“Elevate your political stance, and remain clearheaded and vigilant,” Mr. Chen told them.

“提高政治站位，保持清醒警醒，”陈吉宁对他们说。

储百亮(Chris Buckley)是《纽约时报》首席中国记者，自台北报道中国和台湾问题，重点关注政治、社会变革以及安全和军事问题。

2026年11月25日

item.title: 申包胥哭秦庭：救楚之后，为何又逃掉了封赏
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

春秋末年，楚国有两个关系很深的人，一个叫伍员，后来人称伍子胥；另一个叫申包胥。

两人的人生最终走向了完全相反的方向。

伍子胥的父兄被楚平王杀害，他逃离楚国。临走时，他曾对申包胥说：“我必覆楚。”申包胥回答：“勉之。子能覆之，我必能兴之。”

这几句话见于《左传》。当时或许谁也想不到，两个人后来竟真的各自兑现了自己的诺言。

伍子胥逃到吴国后受到重用。公元前506年，吴王阖闾大举攻楚，吴军在柏举之战中击败楚军，继而攻入楚国都城郢。楚昭王仓皇出逃，最后避难于随国。立国数百年的楚国，一度到了亡国边缘。

这时，申包胥想起了自己当年说过的话。

他赶到秦国，请求秦哀公出兵救楚。

申包胥并没有只向秦国诉说楚国有多可怜。他提出的实际上是一套相当现实的利害分析：吴国如同“封豕长蛇”，贪得无厌，如今先吞楚国；一旦楚国灭亡，吴国势力继续西进，秦国也将直接面对吴国。与其等吴国坐大，不如现在救楚，使楚国成为秦国东方的屏障。

这番话并没有立即打动秦哀公。

秦哀公让人告诉申包胥：“你的意思我已经知道了，先到馆舍休息，我们商量之后再答复。”

申包胥却回答：“我的国君现在还流落草野，没有安身之处，我怎么敢自己去安歇？”

于是发生了中国历史上著名的“哭秦庭”。

《左传》记载，申包胥站在秦国宫廷的墙边痛哭，“日夜不绝声，勺饮不入口七日”。他整整七天不离开，也几乎不进饮食。

七天之后，秦哀公终于改变了主意。

他为申包胥赋《诗经·秦风》中的《无衣》。那首诗写的是同仇敌忾、整顿兵甲、共同出征。申包胥明白秦君已经决定发兵，于是九次叩首。

“秦师乃出。”

第二年，秦国大夫子蒲、子虎率兵车五百乘进入楚国，与楚军共同对吴作战。吴军随后连续遭到反击，加上吴国内部发生变化，最终退出楚境。流亡在外的楚昭王重新回到郢都。

申包胥当初那句“我必能兴之”，终于实现了。

楚昭王复国以后，开始奖赏那些在国家危亡中立下功劳的大臣，申包胥自然名列其中。无论从哪一方面说，他都完全有资格接受重赏：楚国几乎灭亡，是他远赴秦国求援；秦国原本犹豫不决，又是他哭秦庭七日，终于促使秦国出兵。

然而申包胥拒绝了。

《左传》记下了他的回答：“吾为君也，非为身也。君既定矣，又何求？”

意思很简单：我做这些事情是为了国君、为了国家，并不是为了自己。如今君位已经安定，我还有什么可求的？

随后《左传》只用了三个字：“遂逃赏。”

他干脆躲掉了赏赐。

后来的《新序》把这个故事写得更加完整，说申包胥认为，救国家危难并不是为了个人名声，如果事情做成之后再领取重赏，就仿佛是在出售自己的勇气。不过这些话属于后世进一步整理的叙述，《左传》留下的那句“君既定矣，又何求”，其实已经足够。

申包胥最特别的地方，也许并不只是忠于楚国。

春秋时代忠臣很多，临危赴难的人也并不少见。真正让这个人物显得不同的，是他把“做事”与“取利”分得极开。

国家危亡时，他不等别人催促，自己跑到秦国求援；秦国不肯发兵，他就站在庭中哭了七天；事情成功之后，楚王要给他报偿，他反而走了。

他并不是不知道自己的功劳有多大。

恰恰因为知道，所以更不肯把这件事变成一笔交易。

两千五百多年以后再看申包胥，最有意味的还是他与伍子胥当年的那场对话。

一个说：“我必覆楚。”

一个说：“我必兴之。”

后来伍子胥真的率吴军打进郢都，申包胥也真的从秦国搬来了救兵。

两个人各行其志，各自完成了自己许下的话。

而申包胥做到最后，又悄然离开了封赏。

历史因此记住了他。

资料来源：《左传·定公四年》《左传·定公五年》；另参考刘向《新序·节士》。

item.title: 两次高考，我终于进了大学
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

我参加过两次高考。

第一次是1977年。考试时间是12月11日至13日，我的准考证号是771274。那一年高考刚刚恢复，准考证上还特别注明：“实行开卷考试。考生只允许带初、高中课本和十一大文件。”

当时我已经在韶关市第五中学教语文，一边上课，一边复习。最后没有被录取，不是因为成绩，而是体检出了问题。

那年冬天我一直坚持冬泳。1978年元旦，我还横渡过武江，当天气温只有2摄氏度。高考复习期间我也照游不误，直到体检发现肺部“有阴影”，才停下来。我随后到韶关、广州几家医院复查，结果都正常，但那时参加考试的人太多，我的复查材料没有改变结果。

那一年，我们学校有几位年轻教师考上了大学。一个和我一起在海南农场劳动过的高中同学也考进华南师范学院。高考复习时他曾到五中找我，我把自己手上的一些课本给了他。

1978年，我本来已经不太想再考了。

从海南农场调到韶关中学以后，我对现状已经很满足。第一次高考又没录取，更有些“乐不思蜀”。是母亲坚持让我再试一次，她希望我能够考回广州。

于是，我第二次走进考场。

1978年的高考在7月20日至22日举行。我的准考证号是200829。准考证上还有一句今天看起来很特别的规定：如果考生在规定时间内答不完，可以适当延长，但最多不得超过30分钟。

我的成绩是：政治79分，语文81分，数学70分，历史65.5分，地理63.5分，总分359分。外语考俄语，27.8分，只作参考，不计总分。

8月25日，韶关市招生委员会通知我参加体检。通知上写得很有那个年代的味道：“要服从国家利益，坚决服从国家的分配”；即使达到分数线，也只是进入初选，因为参加体检的人数是招生人数的150%，还要做到“一颗红心，两种准备”。

1978年10月，我终于收到录取通知，进入广州师范学院中文系1978级。

学校当时刚刚恢复不久，录取时还叫“广州市教师进修学院”，入学时已经改名广州师范学院。学校没有自己的校舍，暂时借住在东山区广州市第五十七中学。中文、历史、英语等文科系挤在一栋楼里，图书馆也不过是一间大课室。

条件简单，可对我们来说，能够重新坐进课堂已经很难得。

我们班一共44人，其中22人有过上山下乡经历。有人当了整整十年知青才考进大学。我原来已经当过中学教师，在班里年龄也偏大，入学后被推为学习委员，这一当就是四年。

老师大都四五十岁，不少也是从中学调来的。十年动乱刚刚结束，教学科研受到很大影响，课程内容未必都新，教学方法也谈不上丰富，可我们坐在课堂上仍然觉得新鲜。

上现代文学，听老师讲朱自清的《荷塘月色》；上古代汉语，认真默写李白的《梦游天姥吟留别》。大家年龄差距很大，有些人已经结婚成家，却很少缺课。

对我最困难的是英语。

我中学学的是俄语，进大学以后却要从ABC重新学起。班里大部分同学原来学过英语，我只好一点一点追。兴趣倒很高，考试分数也不差，不过真正学到多少，自己心里明白。

大学期间，我第一次参加所谓“科研”，是和同学一起编写《中学语文词语语法修辞例句选》。大家课外翻资料、找例句，那已经是另一种完全不同于农场生活的日子。

四年以后，我大学毕业并留校任教。

后来，一位当年参加招生工作的处长告诉我一个我此前不知道的情况：1978级有几个考生分数并不低，只是年龄偏大，其他学校没有录取。广州师范学院当时觉得，如果再不把这些人招回来，他们可能就再也没有机会回广州了，于是把我们录取了。

听到这句话时，我才真正意识到，自己当年离大学校门，其实并没有想象中那么远。

第一次高考，因为体检问题错过；第二次再考，年龄又已经偏大。若不是母亲坚持让我再试一次，也许我早已安心留在韶关当中学教师。

1978年秋天，我终于走进了大学校门。

那一步，对后来的人生意味着什么，是很多年以后才真正明白的。

资料来源：崔干行《我终于走进大学校门》；本文据原文整理改写。

item.title: “文革没有腐败”为什么站不住脚
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

一种常见说法是，“文革”时期干部收入不高，也没有今天动辄千万、上亿元的贪腐案件，因此那是一个“没有腐败”的年代。

这种比较忽略了一个基本事实：腐败的规模，首先受整个社会财富规模制约。

一个普遍贫困、商品短缺的社会，本来就不可能产生今天这种规模的权钱交易。一名基层干部利用职权多吃几顿饭、多拿一些紧俏商品、为亲友安排一个好工作，折算成今天的钱可能微不足道，但在当时却可能意味着十分明显的特权。

有关毛泽东时代农村政治的研究也发现，大跃进以后，农村干部中的受贿、侵占和利用职位谋取私利已经成为实际问题；一些生产大队干部可以通过工作分、集体福利、工作机会分配等方式获得利益，也存在接受礼品以换取行政照顾的情况。

“文革”并没有消灭产生腐败的条件。相反，在许多地方，政治运动破坏了正常制度，而基层干部对劳动分配、工作安排、政治鉴定乃至个人前途仍掌握相当大的裁量权。

因此，判断一个年代有没有腐败，不能简单比较受贿金额。

真正应该问的是：一个掌握公共权力的人，能不能利用这种权力给自己和亲友获得普通人得不到的东西；一个普通人为了避免被刁难或者获得正常机会，是否不得不送礼、托关系。

按照这个标准，“文革没有腐败”很难成立。

它更多意味着：那个年代很穷，所以腐败也常常以贫穷年代的方式存在。

一顿饭里的权力：文革农村的“防御性送礼”

在物质极度匮乏的年代，基层腐败未必表现为现金交易，有时只是一顿饭、一包烟、一瓶酒。

一些“文革”亲历者回忆，农村生产队长虽然只是最基层的小干部，却掌握着派工、记工分以及许多日常事务。谁家的劳动安排轻一些，谁容易被挑毛病，很多时候都与队干部的态度有关。

于是，一些地方形成了特殊的人情规则：家里来了客人，桌上难得有一点好菜，也要请队长来“陪客”。开始可能只是有人主动巴结，时间久了，却逐渐成为别人不得不遵守的规矩。

这种送礼有一个特点：农民未必希望从干部那里获得额外利益，只希望不要受到额外伤害。

不送，不一定失去一项本该没有的好处，却可能在派工、劳动评价或者日常生活中受到刁难。因此，一顿饭、一包好烟的作用，不是“请你帮我”，而是“请你不要整我”。

这种现象可以称为“防御性行贿”。

历史研究也显示，人民公社时期一些基层干部利用工作分、集体福利、就业岗位以及行政决定获得礼物和其他好处。生产大队干部尤其拥有大量贴近日常生活的裁量空间。

这类腐败金额很小，却有一个很值得注意的特点：它发生在普通人无法避开的日常生活中。

一个掌握巨大财政预算的高官，离普通农民也许很遥远；一个能够决定你明天去哪里干活、给你记多少工分的生产队长，却每天就在身边。

所以，小权力并不天然意味着小伤害。

当权力缺少可以真正制约它的规则时，哪怕只是一个生产队长，也足以让一顿原本属于自家的好饭变成必须付出的“保护费”。

不用考试以后：工农兵学员招生中的“走后门”

“文革”期间，高考停止。1970年以后，高校逐步恢复招生，实行工农兵学员制度，基本原则是“自愿报考、群众推荐、领导批准、学校复查”。

这个制度原本强调政治表现和劳动实践，希望改变单纯依靠考试选拔学生的方式。但一个很快出现的问题是：当统一考试取消以后，谁能够得到推荐，便变成了一项十分重要的权力。

中国科学院有关恢复高考历史的资料明确指出，由于招生不进行公开考试，推荐和批准环节“走后门”现象严重，而且屡禁不止。

南京大学档案保存的材料尤其典型。1972年，中共中央专门发出《关于杜绝高等学校招生工作中“走后门”现象的通知》。后来南京大学工农兵学员钟志民公开承认，自己就是通过父亲打电话给部队干部部门，指名调动后进入大学。1974年，《人民日报》甚至刊登了他的退学申请，把这件事作为反对“走后门”的典型。

这件事本身已经说明问题。

如果“群众推荐”能够天然保证公平，中央就没有必要专门发布文件反对走后门，更不会出现全国宣传的退学典型。

在一个缺乏统一、公开、可量化竞争标准的招生制度中，推荐权本身就成为稀缺资源。一个青年能不能上大学，不仅取决于个人能力，还可能取决于家庭背景、领导关系以及谁有能力影响推荐程序。

1977年恢复高考以后，考试重新成为大学招生的主要入口。它当然并非完美制度，却至少重新确立了一条所有考生都可以看到的规则：考卷相同，分数可以比较，决定一个人前途的权力不再主要掌握在某个单位领导的一句话里。

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia flying to Spain after months of U.S. deportation efforts
item.description:
Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year and sent to a notorious prison in his home country, is planning to leave the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, according to multiple U.S. officials familiar with the matter.

Abrego Garcia, whose case became an early flashpoint in the debate over the Trump administration's deportation crackdown, is set to fly to Spain on a commercial flight Tuesday, according to the sources, who requested anonymity to talk about an arrangement that has not been disclosed publicly.

The exact nature of his arrangements and the conditions of his departure from the U.S. were not immediately clear. But the federal judge in Maryland overseeing his civil legal case issued an order Friday that remains sealed.

CBS News has reached out to an attorney and representatives for Abrego Garcia.

The move by Abrego Garcia comes after the Trump administration spent months trying to deport the man, who came to the U.S. illegally 15 years ago and had been living in Maryland with his wife and children when he was detained by immigration authorities in March 2025. He was then deported to El Salvador and held for months in the country's CECOT prison, despite a previous court order barring him from being sent back to his home country. He was brought back to the United States last year to face criminal charges.

Abrego Garcia has maintained for more than a year that if he had to leave the U.S. again, he would be willing to go to Costa Rica, and designated the Central American nation as his preferred country of removal.

But the Trump administration had resisted that suggestion and instead unsuccessfully sought to deport Abrego Garcia to numerous African countries, including Uganda, Eswatini and Ghana. In more recent months, the Department of Homeland Security said it was ready to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia — part of a broader practice of sending deportees to countries in Africa.

Abrego Garcia's departure from the U.S. came weeks after a hearing before U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis, who has been presiding over a civil case stemming from his deportation last year, was abruptly cancelled. The judge ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement last year to release Abrego Garcia from immigration custody and has continued to bar immigration authorities from detaining him while litigation continued.

But the Trump administration had sought to lift Xinis' orders, which it said were the only impediments to Abrego Garcia's "prompt removal." The Justice Department said in March that the government was "ready, willing, and able" to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia in West Africa.

Abrego Garcia's case gained national prominence last year after a top administration official acknowledged that his removal to El Salvador was an "error." Following his arrest by immigration authorities in March 2025, Abrego Garcia was among the more than 200 immigrants who were sent to El Salvador and detained at its notorious supermax prison, the Terrorism Confinement Center, or CECOT.

But Abrego Garcia had been granted a withholding of removal by an immigration judge in 2019, which prevented immigration authorities from deporting him to his home country of El Salvador because he was at risk of persecution by local gangs. 

In April 2025, Xinis ordered the Department of Homeland Security to bring Abrego Garcia back to the U.S., and the Supreme Court said the government had to facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody.

The Trump administration ultimately brought Abrego Garcia back to the U.S. in June 2025, but only after he was indicted on federal charges of human smuggling stemming from a 2022 traffic stop in Tennessee. Abrego Garcia pleaded not guilty and in May, a federal judge in Tennessee dismissed the criminal charges on the grounds that his prosecution was vindictive. 

The Justice Department has appealed that decision, and arguments before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit are scheduled for February.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kilmar-abrego-garcia-leaving-us-europe/

item.title: 一针直降百万，这款天价抗癌药经历了什么？
Search is on for 4 adults and 2 children after plane crashes off Mississippi coast
item.description:
Authorities are searching for six people after a plane crashed into the water northeast of Horn Island, Mississippi, on Tuesday afternoon, the US Coast Guard said.

There were four adults and two children aboard the Cessna Centurion 210 aircraft, according to the agency.

The US Coast Guard received a call around 3:45 p.m. Tuesday after the FAA lost communication with the aircraft, a spokesperson for the US Coast Guard Mobile told CNN.

Crews searching the scene have so far found three life jackets, a life raft and the cabin of the aircraft, the spokesperson added.

Flight tracking data shows the Cessna 210 was flying from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida.

About 30 minutes after take off, while it was at about 8,800 feet in the air, just south of Pascagoula, Mississippi, the plane suddenly plunged toward the water, according to the website Flightradar24. The aircraft was diving at 18,000 feet a minute, more than 200 miles per hour, in the final seconds before the tracking data ceases.

The National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation into the crash, according to the Federal Aviation Administration, which will also be assisting in the probe. The US Coast Guard is on scene along with the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources and local agencies.

Horn Island is a remote, undeveloped island about 12 nautical miles from Biloxi, Mississippi, that is only accessible by private boat. The journey from nearby Biloxi, Ocean Springs or Pascagoula takes about 30 minutes to an hour.

The island is part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore, a national park that includes a dozen islands stretching 160 miles across Mississippi and Florida.

Horn Island is about 10 miles long and only about a mile wide. It is a popular summer destination for state residents.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Alisha Ebrahimji contributed to this report.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

item.title: 观点：中国即将迎来人工智能恐慌，等着瞧吧
item.description:
面对国内威胁，中国中央政府向来倾向于迅速采取强硬手段。 马云的遭遇并非孤例。今年6月，一架小型飞机撞上北京最高的建筑。如今，北京周边划定了面积相当于整个意大利的禁飞区，几乎所有私人飞行活动都被禁止。 2023年，上海一名脱口秀演员拿中国人民解放军的口号当作笑料。此后，全国各地的脱口秀俱乐部纷纷取消演出，持续了数月。如今，脱口秀演员在登台前，往往必须将演出文稿提交审查。 与中国近年来更为严厉的镇压和管控行动相比，这些还只是小事。我想到的是维吾尔族等少数民族和宗教群体的成员遭到拘禁，以及2022年春天，为了阻止新冠病毒传播，拥有2500万人口的上海禁止居民离开各自居住的小区。 中国政府不会对潜在威胁表现出多少容忍，尤其是在未来12个月。我们正在进入中国政治日程中最敏感的阶段，也就是中共全国代表大会召开前夕。 明年秋天，中国最高领导人习近平很可能为自己开启第四个五年任期。在这样的时期，中共对社会不稳定因素的容忍度会更低。 人工智能一旦闯出大祸，中国政府也不会全面禁止这项技术。中国政府太多部门都寄望于人工智能推动经济增长、增强地缘政治实力。 根据危机的性质，中国政府最有可能加强监控，并限制人工智能的普及和使用。政府也可能进一步掌控人工智能的开发过程，而不是继续让DeepSeek这样的民营企业主导技术发展。 习近平已经表明，为了维持社会稳定，他愿意牺牲相当程度的经济增长。 事实上，在人工智能竞赛中，中国政府并非始终全速前进。中国限制进口为最先进人工智能系统提供算力的英伟达芯片，就反映出北京试图在提升本国人工智能实力与扶持中国芯片制造商之间取得平衡。

item.title: 〖微博谈〗老黄逼着全世界人看了一集红果短剧
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

（所有图片均来自网络）

1．@Jalen20260216：人类社会的基本常识：上学是为了启迪思想。但在中国和朝鲜这些地方，上学却是为了禁锢思想。

2．@dajiyuan：印尼海军公布了一起海上走私案件，一艘据报从中国连云港出发、驶往孟加拉国的货轮遭扣押，船上载有405吨可用于制造导弹推进剂的高氯酸钠，以及数百万张空白SIM卡。此次查获的高氯酸钠数量，相当于孟加拉国近17年进口总量的约591倍。这批材料可能足以制造100枚导弹。然而，孟加拉国海关表示，未收到这艘货轮的进口申报文件，也无法确认其当地船务代理商的身份。

3．@dayangelcp：真是杀疯了。一年抓了四个政治局委员：何卫东、张又侠、马兴瑞、陈吉宁。而且二十年来，第一个上海市委书记被抓。论年均清洗速度，已经超过了刘彻和崇祯，也就斯大林同志能压一头。不过也快了，习惯性清洗跟习惯性脱臼一样的，开始有点痛，后来成为生活的一部分。赫鲁晓夫同志在哪呢？

4．【闭环】美股大跌——我们受外围市场影响，大跌。美股大涨——我们资金都被外围市场吸走，大跌。

5．@dao_wan73049：我想了三天三夜没想明白，35岁找工作嫌你老，65岁退休嫌你小，中间这三十年叫：人口红利。红利本人怎么不知道？

6．60天账期喊破了喉咙，车企供应商仍是望眼欲穿。

7．财新何意味？

8．书荼门人：【给环卫工人佩戴电子工牌】这种电子工牌有定位功能，以及在环卫工人“静止不动”的时候会提醒他们。但被用于宣传的，还是它的SOS紧急求助功能。也就是说，你不能说他们这是用来监视环卫工人的。他们的主要目的还是为了保护环卫工人，万一身体有什么不舒服，按一下那个SOS键，就能迅速得到帮助。

9．恶意对比。

10．@lisiyu0671：老黄逼着全世界人看了一集红果短剧。

item.title: 〖微视野〗我心无我亦无君
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

（所有图片均来自网络）

1．元稹：终须修到无修处，闻尽声闻始不闻。莫着妄心销彼我，我心无我亦无君。

2．刘耿：日语里还有一些这样的词：晚秋初冬，一阵细雨飘过，地皮刚湿，雨又歇了，叫“时雨”；春日花落，残瓣聚在溪面上，连缀成片，随波缓缓漂流，叫“花筏”；入冬前后，吹得树叶凋零的寒风，叫“木枯”；连树干上留下的一只蝉蜕，也有个名字，叫“空蝉”。它们借着风物的名字，把人那一刻的微妙感觉也一并收了进去。

3．@推拿熊：我看短剧最重要的痛点就是绝大多数人认为人生最好的解决办法就是重新投胎，因为这破地球，生存类游戏打到三四十岁了还真跟王勃说的一样三尺微命。一介书生时运不济命运多舛关山难越谁悲失路之人萍水相逢尽是他乡之客，这玩意儿真得信命，不信书，信运气，不如直接重开得了。

4．@elonmusk：Everyone is your friend when the chips are up，but those who support you when the chips are down are your real friends. Fair-weather friends are worthless.

5．@Luellen1M：I'm getting into it.

6．@lazzzy_42：猫猫牌温度计。

7．游戏嘛，都是体验下现实里没有的。

8．茨冈女神：古人酿酒，多以春字为名。南宋周密的《武林旧事》记有“皇都春”、“留都春”、“秦淮春”、“海岳春”、“丰和春”、“蓬莱春”等。见于唐宋诗词中的也有“金陵春”、“洞庭春”、“曲来春”、“木兰春”、“中山春”等酒名。酒以“春”为名，大概是源于《诗经•七月》中“为此春酒，以介眉寿”之句。古时春天饮的酒，大都是冬天酿造的，故认为春酒可延年益寿。如今大概只有一个剑南春了？

9．【人的味觉和心情是连着的】看甜剧时吃甜食，真的会觉得“更甜”。美国《媒体心理学》杂志一项研究发现，当味觉体验和剧集情节匹配时，观众更容易感受到主人公的情绪。这可能是因为大脑处理味觉的区域和情绪、共情区域联系紧密。当味觉和情绪会互相呼应、彼此放大，会让当下的感受更强烈。

10．【对心脏来说，泡脚是一把“双刃剑”】泡对了有助“稳心”，泡错了反而会加重心脏负担。温水舒活血管，改善末梢循环。身体温热放松后，交感神经紧张度下降，人身心舒缓，但如果水温过高，时间过长，反而会给心脏增加负担。

item.title: 外交政策：美国官方和媒体如何粉饰以色列的种族灭绝行为
item.description:
苏茜·汉森在《外交政策》杂志撰文，通过《跨越红线》和《不要说巴勒斯坦》两本新书，探讨拜登政府与西方主流媒体如何利用语言掩盖加沙战争的残酷现实，以及美国的政治体制、外交政策和新闻报道如何共同为以色列的军事行动提供正当性。 《不要说巴勒斯坦》的作者、中东历史学者阿萨尔·拉德，通过分析《纽约时报》、BBC、路透社等媒体的新闻标题，揭示西方媒体如何使用被动语态、委婉措辞和缺乏历史背景的叙事，淡化以色列的责任。例如，将强制驱逐巴勒斯坦人描述为普通的房屋驱逐纠纷，将无差别轰炸称为“定点打击”，将蓄意制造饥饿描述为“人道主义挑战”。相比之下，西方媒体在报道乌克兰发生的类似暴行时，通常会明确指出俄罗斯或普京的责任。拉德认为，媒体对以色列官方说法的过度依赖，不仅误导了公众，也使美国政府更加难以正视自身政策造成的灾难。 记者阿克巴尔·沙希德·艾哈迈德的《跨越红线》则通过调查报道，揭示拜登政府内部的决策过程。书中披露，拜登的外交政策团队绕过国会监督和正常行政程序，压制政府内部的反对意见，利用法律解释规避对以色列战争罪行的认定，并质疑人道主义机构和情报部门对加沙饥荒的评估。即使以色列不断破坏停火谈判、扩大军事行动，拜登政府仍然持续提供武器。美国甚至不惜耗费资源修建海上码头和空投食品，却不愿直接向以色列施压，要求开放正常的人道主义援助渠道。 汉森认为，拜登政府的政策失误不仅源于个人政治利益、官僚体系中的群体思维以及对以色列根深蒂固的情感认同，更涉及美国外交政策长期存在的种族偏见。数十年来，美国一直致力于确保以色列拥有中东地区的军事优势，而加沙战争最终暴露了这一战略所付出的人道主义代价。 文章还批评拜登政府前官员在卸任后继续逃避责任，仿佛他们作为世界上最强大国家的决策者，既无法约束内塔尼亚胡，也无法影响拜登本人。汉森认为，美国和以色列政治体系中形成的共识共同破坏了国际法律秩序，而西方主流媒体长期以来以谨慎、模糊和所谓客观的语言记录这一过程，却未能充分履行新闻业最重要的职责：监督权力，追究掌权者的责任。
